title: Governance & repo constitution: make CandleViewer governable from commit #1
body:
## Context

CandleViewer is a private, self-hosted trading terminal built by ~15 engineers plus a large design org on 2-week sprints starting 2026-09-25 (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`). Every later epic (E02 monorepo, E03 CI/CD, … E49) assumes that the repository is *already* governed: a ratified constitution, enforced code ownership, DoR/DoD gates, a board schema with automation, and branch protection that makes an ungoverned merge impossible.

`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 places this epic first in R0 with 21 points in Sprint 01 and states the intent plainly: "governance epics land day 1–3 so all later work is compliant" (§4.5). The epic dependency graph (§11.1) makes E01 the root: `E01 --> E02 --> E03`. R0 exit criterion #1 is owned entirely by this epic: "`main` is protected; no path in the repo is un-owned by CODEOWNERS; a PR without 2 approvals incl. a code-owner is demonstrably unmergeable."

Most governance *documents* already exist in the working tree as drafts (`CONSTITUTION.md` 1091 lines, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`). This epic's job is therefore not "write docs from a blank page" — it is to **ratify, reconcile, machine-verify and enforce** them: eliminate drift between the constitution and its satellites (C-16.5 single-source-of-truth registry), make every rule reference resolvable (C-16.4), make ownership total, publish the backlog ticket schema the whole planning phase depends on, wire the board automation the DoD assumes, and turn branch protection on.

Related plan docs: `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (branching, board Status semantics, labels, review rules, estimation), `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` (per-Kind DoR/DoD gates this epic automates), `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 (black-box QA process, test-plan-in-ticket convention), `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13–§6.14 (supply chain, CI secrets), `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (AA target incl. contributor-facing surfaces we control), `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (release/PRR gates that read the board).

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Constitution ratified and self-verifying** — `CONSTITUTION.md` v1.0.0, amendment log, rule-id link-check script, C-16.5 de-duplication sweep across all tracked docs (E01-T01).
- **Satellite governance docs reconciled** — `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `AGENTS.md` aligned to the constitution with zero duplicated single-source lists (E01-T02).
- **`SECURITY.md`** — vulnerability reporting, supported versions, private-repo threat context, coordinated-disclosure timeline (E01-T03).
- **`.github/CODEOWNERS` total coverage** + `scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.*` proving no tracked path is un-owned (E01-T04).
- **PR template + issue forms** refreshed to the taxonomy in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5 (Kind, area/*, priority/*, cross-cutting labels) (E01-T05).
- **Backlog ticket schema** published at `docs/plan/backlog/schema/` (owned artefact per C-16.5) + a validator run over every `docs/plan/backlog/*.json` (E01-T06).
- **Board automation** — GitHub Actions implementing label↔Kind sync, QA-sign-off gate, security-close guard, a11y run-link guard, design-ahead warning (E01-T07).
- **Branch protection & merge queue as code** — required checks exactly matching `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 table, 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner, linear history, conversation resolution (E01-T08).
- **Spike** on GitHub Projects v2 automation capability and its limits (E01-K01).
- **Design** of the contributor information architecture and issue forms, plus a design-QA/a11y pass on the rendered GitHub surfaces (E01-D01, E01-D02).
- **QA** governance conformance test plan + exploratory charter, and an automated governance regression pack (E01-Q01, E01-Q02).
- **Security** STRIDE threat model for the repo/CI/board administration surface and a review of every automation workflow's token scopes (E01-X01, E01-X02).

No product screens (SCR-*), components (CMP-*), user stories (US-*), API paths, WS topics or DB tables are introduced by this epic — its surface is the repository, the GitHub project board, and CI metadata. The `domains` and `modules` columns for E01 in `30-release-roadmap.md` §3 are both `—` for exactly this reason.

## Out of scope

- The CI pipeline itself (workflow jobs `lint`, `unit-*`, `contract`, `sast`, …) — owned by **E03**; E01 only *names and requires* those checks in branch protection and fails loudly if a named check does not exist.
- Monorepo layout, tooling config, `import-linter` contracts — owned by **E02** (the constitution §3 module edges are authored here, encoded there).
- Any product design-system work (tokens, components) — owned by **E05**.
- Android, a separate admin app, additional exchanges — permanently out of scope per `CONSTITUTION.md` §1.3 and the owner decision of 2026-09-14.
- Writing the sprint plan `31-sprint-plan.md` — a planning-phase deliverable tracked outside this epic.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: An ungoverned merge is impossible
  Given main branch protection is applied from the committed configuration
  And a pull request touching services/api has only 1 approving review
  When the author attempts to merge or enqueue the PR
  Then GitHub refuses the merge citing missing required reviews
  And the same PR with 2 approvals of which none is a CODEOWNER of services/api is also refused

Scenario: No path in the repository is un-owned
  Given every tracked file path in the repository
  When scripts/check-codeowners-coverage is executed
  Then it exits 0 and reports 0 un-owned paths
  And introducing a new top-level directory without a CODEOWNERS rule makes the same script exit non-zero

Scenario: Every constitution rule reference resolves
  Given all tracked *.md, *.yml, *.yaml files and .github/CODEOWNERS
  When the C-x.y link-check from CONSTITUTION.md C-16.4 runs
  Then it prints no DANGLING RULE REFERENCE line
  And deliberately introducing a reference to a non-existent rule C-99.9 makes it fail

Scenario: A Story cannot be closed without QA sign-off (failure path)
  Given an issue with Kind=Story and no QA sign-off comment or checked sign-off box
  When a maintainer closes the issue
  Then the board automation reopens it (or posts a blocking comment and re-labels it needs-qa-signoff)
  And an audit-trail comment names the missing DoD item from docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §3.2

Scenario: Every backlog ticket file validates against the published schema
  Given docs/plan/backlog/schema/ticket.schema.json
  When the validator runs over every docs/plan/backlog/*.json
  Then all files validate with zero errors
  And a ticket missing the required field "perspective" fails validation with a pointer to the offending key
```

## Technical notes / design

Governance is enforced in four layers, deliberately redundant because any single layer can be bypassed:

1. **Documented rule** — `CONSTITUTION.md` (`C-x.y`, stable ids, never renumbered per C-16.4).
2. **Machine check** — a script in `scripts/` runnable locally and by CI (`pr-metadata` job, §9 #20) that fails on violation.
3. **Platform enforcement** — branch protection, required checks, CODEOWNERS, merge queue.
4. **Board automation** — GitHub Actions reacting to issue/PR events implementing the DoD gates from `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`.

Key invariants:
- **C-16.5 single-source-of-truth registry** — required-check names live only in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9; command names only in `AGENTS.md` §4; directory ownership only in `.github/CODEOWNERS`; ticket schema only in `docs/plan/backlog/schema/`. Every satellite document links rather than restates. The de-dup checker is part of `pr-metadata`.
- **Fail-closed automation** — a guard workflow that errors (API failure, rate limit) must block, not silently pass; every guard writes an explicit success/failure comment so the state is auditable.
- **Least-privilege tokens** — workflows declare `permissions:` explicitly at job level; no `write-all`; no `pull_request_target` with checkout of untrusted refs (see E01-X02).

Configuration keys/artefacts introduced: `.github/workflows/board-automation.yml`, `.github/workflows/governance-checks.yml`, `.github/branch-protection.json` (applied by a documented idempotent script), `docs/plan/backlog/schema/ticket.schema.json`, `scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py`, `scripts/check-rule-refs.sh`, `scripts/check-sot-duplication.py`, `scripts/validate-backlog.py`.

Error codes for governance scripts (stable, referenced by CI annotations): `GOV-001` un-owned path, `GOV-002` dangling rule reference, `GOV-003` duplicated single-source list, `GOV-004` backlog schema violation, `GOV-005` required check name mismatch vs §9 table, `GOV-006` missing DoD gate on close.

## Test plan

- **Unit** — each `scripts/*` checker has pytest/bats cases for: clean repo (exit 0), each seeded violation class (exit non-zero with the right `GOV-00n` code), and malformed input (no traceback leak).
- **Contract** — the ticket JSON schema is exercised against a golden valid ticket and a matrix of one-field-missing / wrong-enum-value invalid tickets.
- **Integration** — board automation is tested against a scratch repository (or `act` + mocked GitHub API) covering label sync, close-guard trip, and guard-error fail-closed behaviour.
- **E2E (manual, recorded)** — the branch-protection acceptance scenarios executed once against the real repo with screenshots attached to E01-Q01.
- **Regression pack** — E01-Q02 wires all of the above into a single `governance` CI job that runs on every PR.
- Coverage target: ≥85% line coverage on `scripts/` (treated as backend Python per `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #3).

## Security notes

Threat surface: repository and CI administration (STRIDE areas adjacent to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9/§6.13–§6.14 supply chain and CI secrets). Principal threats: (T) tampering with governance files or branch protection to smuggle unreviewed code; (E) privilege escalation via an over-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` in a board-automation workflow; (E/T) `pull_request_target` pwn-request allowing a fork PR to execute with write privileges; (R) repudiation if protection is disabled and re-enabled without an audit trail; (I) disclosure of the private repo's existence/content via a misconfigured template or public issue form.

Controls: CODEOWNERS on `/CONSTITUTION.md`, `/.github/`, `/.github/workflows/` requiring security-team review; explicit least-privilege `permissions:` blocks; pinned action SHAs; no secrets in fork-triggered workflows; branch protection stored as code so drift is detectable. Data classification: **public-internal metadata only** — no secrets, PII or financial data. Security review label required (E01-X01, E01-X02 carry the sign-off).

## Accessibility notes

This epic ships no application UI, but it does own contributor-facing surfaces we control: GitHub issue **forms** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`) and the markdown governance docs. Requirements: every issue-form field has a real `label` (never placeholder-as-label); required fields are marked programmatically; markdown uses a single H1 and a correctly nested heading hierarchy so screen-reader document navigation works; every mermaid diagram in a governance doc is preceded or followed by a prose summary conveying the same information (diagrams are inaccessible images when rendered); tables have header rows; no information is conveyed by colour alone. Verified in E01-D02 against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes

No runtime performance budget applies (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets are product budgets). One process budget does apply and is asserted in E01-Q02: the **governance checks job must complete in ≤60 s** so it never becomes the long pole in the ≤15 min commit-to-dev pipeline required by R0 exit criterion #2.

## Observability

- Every governance script emits structured, greppable output (`GOV-00n <path> <detail>`) and GitHub Actions annotations so failures are visible in the PR diff view, not only in raw logs.
- Board-automation workflows post an explicit audit comment on every gate decision (allowed/blocked + which DoD item), giving a permanent, queryable record.
- A weekly scheduled `governance-drift` run compares live branch-protection settings with `.github/branch-protection.json` and opens a `priority/p1-high` issue on drift.

## Estimation & roadmap reconciliation

- **Epic-level sizing (this ticket's `estimate` field): 21 points.** Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 an Epic carries a *rough* epic-level sizing (T-shirt / 13-point scale) for roadmap placement — not a mechanical roll-up of its children. 21 is the figure budgeted for E01 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 and §4.2, and this field is deliberately kept identical to it so the roadmap and the board never disagree.
- **Child roll-up: 22 points** (K01 1; T01 2; T02 1; T03 1; T04 1; T05 2; T06 2; T07 3; T08 2; D01 1; D02 1; Q01 1; Q02 1; X01 2; X02 1). That is +4.8% against the 21-point budget, inside the ±15% tolerance (18–24) that `E01-T06`'s validator enforces between a backlog file's child sum and `backlog_epics_seed.json`.
- **What changed and why:** an earlier revision of this file carried a 42-point child roll-up — 100% over budget — because each governance document was sized as if it were greenfield authoring. It is not: `CONSTITUTION.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, the PR template and the existing issue forms **are already in the repository**. T01–T05 are reconciliation, de-duplication and taxonomy alignment against drafted documents, which is materially cheaper than authoring. Estimates were re-baselined on that basis at refinement; the roadmap's 21-point figure stands unchanged, so `30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (E01 = 21), the R0 total of 322 points and the 38-point (11%) R0 buffer are all untouched.
- **Guard against drift:** `E01-T06` fails CI if this epic's child sum leaves the ±15% band, so any future re-estimation of a child forces an explicit roadmap conversation rather than a silent budget overrun.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All child tickets (E01-T01…T08, K01, D01, D02, Q01, Q02, X01, X02) Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion #1 demonstrated live (protected `main`, total ownership, unmergeable under-reviewed PR) with evidence attached.
- [ ] `CONSTITUTION.md` v1.0.0 ratified; amendment log row present; rule-reference link-check clean across the whole tree.
- [ ] Zero duplicated single-source lists (C-16.5) — checker green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/backlog/schema/` published and every `docs/plan/backlog/*.json` validates.
- [ ] Board automation live and demonstrated tripping on a deliberately non-compliant issue.
- [ ] Docs: `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` reconciled with what was actually built (no divergence).
- [ ] a11y: issue forms and governance docs pass the E01-D02 checklist.
- [ ] Security: STRIDE model (E01-X01) finalised, findings triaged, Security-engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] QA sign-off: E01-Q01 test plan executed, exploratory charter debrief attached.
- [ ] Design sign-off: CDO accepts E01-D01 contributor IA.
- [ ] Child point roll-up re-checked at epic close and still within ±15% of the roadmap's 21-point budget (or `30-release-roadmap.md` §3 amended with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Design-ahead waiver for E01-D01 → E01-T05/E01-D02 recorded on those tickets with Architect/CDO names and date, and carried into the R0 retro.
- [ ] Demoed at the Sprint 01 review with Owner acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies

None — E01 is the root of the epic dependency graph (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1). It *blocks* E02 (monorepo scaffold), which blocks E03 (CI/CD) and everything downstream. E01-T08's required-check names are forward references to jobs E03 creates; the branch-protection configuration is authored here and the checks become enforceable as E03 lands them, which is why T08 ships the names plus a `GOV-005` reconciliation check rather than waiting on E03.

## Branch

`feat/gov-constitution-ratify` and siblings `feat/gov-<short>` per child ticket; governance doc edits use `docs(repo):` conventional-commit type. PR size guidance: ≤400 LOC diff; the constitution reconciliation sweep (T01) may exceed this for pure-deletion de-duplication and must state "why this can't be split" per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §6.3.

## References

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Spike: GitHub Projects v2 + Actions automation capability and limits
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2 and §4 assert automation we have not yet proven possible on GitHub Projects v2: "Automation (GitHub Actions) enforces: a Story/Bug cannot move to Done without `qa` sign-off recorded …; a ticket labelled `security` cannot close without a comment from a Security-team member; `a11y`-labelled tickets require a linked axe-core CI run URL." `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 additionally lists "board automation (label↔Kind sync, QA-sign-off bot, security-close guard, a11y run-link guard)" as E01 scope, and `00-planning-brief.md` names a PenniLogic-style field schema (Status, Kind, Phase, Sprint, Component, Priority, Perspective, Risk, Estimate, Start, Due, Rollup, Forecast*).

Projects v2 has real constraints that determine the design of E01-T07 and E01-T08: single-select field options must be created via GraphQL, the classic `projects: write` permission on `GITHUB_TOKEN` does **not** grant Projects v2 access (a PAT or GitHub App installation token is needed), `Status` changes do not emit an issue event that Actions can trigger on in all cases, and org-level vs user-level projects differ (this project is user-level: `https://github.com/users/basiltt/projects/10`). Building T07 on an unverified assumption would burn a Sprint-01-critical path.

## Scope / Deliverables

Answer, with evidence, in a findings document at `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-board-automation.md` (next free ADR number after ADR-0015; add the row to `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` and §16 of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` in the same PR per the ADR README rules):

1. Can an Actions workflow read and write Projects v2 item field values for a **user-level** project, and with which credential (fine-grained PAT stored as a secret vs GitHub App)? What is the minimum scope set?
2. Which events are actually observable: `issues` (opened/labeled/closed/reopened), `projects_v2_item` (edited/created), `issue_comment`? Is a `Status` field change observable, and with what latency?
3. Can a close be *blocked*, or only *compensated* (reopen + comment)? This determines whether the DoD gates in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` are preventive or detective controls.
4. Can the full field schema (Kind, Phase, Sprint, Component, Priority, Perspective, Risk, Estimate, Start, Due, Rollup) be created and populated programmatically, including iteration/date fields?
5. Rate limits and cost for a bulk import of ~1000 backlog tickets from `docs/plan/backlog/*.json` — is a throttled importer needed?
6. Fallback if any of the above is infeasible: which gates move into the `pr-metadata` CI job or into a required PR-template checkbox instead.

**Timebox: 2 days.** Explicitly NOT expected to produce production-shippable code — a throwaway prototype workflow on a scratch repository is the expected artefact.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the production automation (E01-T07).
- Applying branch protection (E01-T08).
- The bulk backlog import itself (a separate follow-up Task filed by this spike if needed).
- Evaluating non-GitHub trackers — the board is locked to GitHub Projects by `00-planning-brief.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Each question is answered with evidence
  Given the six questions listed in Scope
  When the spike timebox ends
  Then each question has a written answer citing a prototype run URL, an API response, or official documentation
  And no answer is stated as an assumption without a marker "UNVERIFIED" plus its risk

Scenario: Close-blocking feasibility is decided
  Given a prototype guard workflow on a scratch repository
  When a Story issue lacking a QA sign-off comment is closed
  Then the observed behaviour (blocked, or reopened-with-comment) is recorded with a screenshot or log
  And ADR-0016 states which control type (preventive/detective) E01-T07 must implement

Scenario: Credential decision is explicit (failure path)
  Given the default GITHUB_TOKEN is used against the user-level project
  When the prototype attempts to update a single-select field value
  Then the failure mode and error message are recorded verbatim
  And ADR-0016 names the chosen credential, its storage location, its scopes, and its rotation owner

Scenario: Import feasibility is quantified
  Given ~1000 synthetic ticket payloads
  When the throughput of item creation + field population is measured
  Then the wall-clock time and any rate-limit responses are recorded
  And a follow-up Task is filed if a throttled/resumable importer is required
```

## Technical notes / design

Probe order (cheapest first): GraphQL `node(id:)` read of the project → `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` mutation → event-trigger matrix by firing each event on a scratch repo and dumping `github.event` → close-guard prototype using `issues: closed` + `gh issue reopen` → bulk-write throughput with a fixed concurrency of 2 and exponential backoff on secondary-rate-limit responses.

Record for each probe: request, response status, latency, and whether a non-default credential was required. Keep the scratch-repo prototype in a branch `spike/gov-projects-automation` and leave it unmerged (Spike DoD, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2).

Decision criteria agreed up front: if close-blocking is impossible **and** compensating reopen latency exceeds 60 s, the QA/security/a11y gates move to the PR-template + `pr-metadata` CI job and the board automation is downgraded to advisory labelling — this is a legitimate outcome, not a failure, and must be reflected back into `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Test plan

Not a shippable-code ticket; verification is evidentiary. Each probe result must be reproducible from the commands recorded in ADR-0016. Any prototype workflow that is later promoted into E01-T07 inherits the Task DoD (unit tests for the guard logic, integration test against a scratch repo).

## Security notes

The credential decision is itself a security decision (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.14 secrets in CI). If a PAT is chosen, record: least-privilege scope set, repository-scoped not account-wide, storage as an Actions secret, rotation interval, and the blast radius if leaked. A GitHub App with an installation token scoped to this repository is preferred and must be recommended unless measured to be infeasible. The spike must not create any long-lived credential in the real repository — scratch repo only. Data classification: no secrets, PII or financial data handled.

## Accessibility notes

N/A — no user interface is produced by this spike.

## Performance notes

One measured budget is required as an output: bulk-import throughput (items/min) and the projected wall-clock for ~1000 tickets, so the import can be scheduled rather than discovered to be a multi-hour job during Sprint 01.

## Observability

title: Ratify CONSTITUTION.md v1.0.0 and make rule references machine-verified
body:
## Context

`CONSTITUTION.md` exists in the working tree (1091 lines, marked "Ratified 2026-09-14 · Version 1.0.0") and declares itself the highest authority in the repository: "Where another document conflicts with the Constitution, the Constitution wins and the other document is a bug to be fixed." Two of its own rules are currently unenforced, which makes the document aspirational rather than binding:

- **C-16.4** requires that every `C-x.y` token cited anywhere in the repository resolves to a `**C-x.y**` declaration in `CONSTITUTION.md`, and states the `pr-metadata` CI job enforces this. That check does not exist yet.
- **C-16.5** establishes a single-source-of-truth registry (rule text, required-check names, perf/bundle budget *values*, command names, repo layout, directory ownership, PR-checklist wording, vulnerability reporting, ticket schema) and says "A PR that copies any of these lists into a second file is rejected". No checker exists, and the plan docs were authored in parallel, so drift is likely already present.

Without these two checks, every downstream ticket that cites a rule id in its acceptance criteria (as `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` encourages) can silently reference a rule that does not exist. This Task closes that gap and formally ratifies the document.

## Scope / Deliverables

- `scripts/check-rule-refs.sh` — extracts every `C-\d+\.\d+` token from all tracked `*.md`, `*.yml`, `*.yaml` files and `.github/CODEOWNERS`, verifies a matching `^\*\*C-x.y\*\*` declaration exists in `CONSTITUTION.md`, prints `GOV-002 <file>:<line> <id>` per violation, exits non-zero on any. (The canonical one-liner is already given verbatim in `CONSTITUTION.md` C-16.4 — productionise it with file:line reporting and a `--fix-suggest` mode that lists the nearest existing ids.)
- `scripts/check-sot-duplication.py` — for each row of the C-16.5 registry table, detect restatement of the owned list outside its owner file using content fingerprints (e.g. ≥3 of the 20 exact required-check names appearing outside `CONSTITUTION.md` §9; ≥3 command names outside `AGENTS.md` §4; budget *values* outside §14). Prints `GOV-003`, exits non-zero. Allowlist file `scripts/sot-allowlist.txt` for legitimate single-name mentions, each entry requiring a one-line justification comment.
- Reconciliation sweep: run both checkers over the current tree and fix every violation found — by deleting the duplicate and linking, or by adding the missing rule declaration. Record the before/after violation counts in the PR description.
- Amendment-log hygiene: confirm the v1.0.0 row exists; document the ratification (approvals per C-16.1 step 4) in the PR.
- Wire both scripts into a `governance` job stub invoked by `pr-metadata` (the job itself is created by E01-Q02; here we only ship the scripts plus a `make governance` / `AGENTS.md` §4 command entry).

## Out of scope

- Rewriting or amending any constitutional rule's *substance* — this Task reconciles and enforces, it does not legislate. A genuine rule gap discovered during the sweep is filed as a separate `constitution`-labelled issue per C-16.1.
- Creating the CI workflow file (E01-Q02 / E03).
- The CODEOWNERS coverage checker (E01-T04) and backlog schema validator (E01-T06), which follow the same script conventions established here.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: A dangling rule reference fails the check
  Given a tracked markdown file citing rule C-99.9 which is not declared in CONSTITUTION.md
  When scripts/check-rule-refs.sh runs
  Then it prints "GOV-002" with the offending file and line number
  And it exits with a non-zero status

Scenario: The current repository is clean after the sweep
  Given the repository at the head of this Task's branch
  When scripts/check-rule-refs.sh and scripts/check-sot-duplication.py both run
  Then both exit 0 and print no GOV-002 or GOV-003 lines

Scenario: A duplicated single-source list is detected
  Given CONTRIBUTING.md is edited to restate five of the required-check names from CONSTITUTION.md section 9
  When scripts/check-sot-duplication.py runs
  Then it prints GOV-003 naming CONTRIBUTING.md and the owning file CONSTITUTION.md section 9
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: A legitimate single mention is not a false positive
  Given a document that mentions exactly one check name in prose while linking to CONSTITUTION.md section 9
  When scripts/check-sot-duplication.py runs
  Then no GOV-003 is reported
  And the allowlist is not required for that case
```

## Technical notes / design

Both scripts are dependency-light Python 3.12 (stdlib only) so they run before any package manager is configured by E02 — a hard constraint, since E01 lands before the monorepo scaffold. `check-rule-refs.sh` may be a thin shell wrapper over the Python implementation for parity with the one-liner published in C-16.4.

File discovery uses `git ls-files` (tracked files only) so that untracked scratch files and vendored directories never trip the checks.

Duplication detection is fingerprint-based, not fuzzy: for each owned list, a small set of exact literal tokens is defined in `scripts/sot-registry.json` (e.g. `{"owner": "CONSTITUTION.md", "section": "9", "tokens": ["unit-backend", "secrets-scan", "container-scan", "engine-bench", "generated-code-check", "pr-metadata", ...], "threshold": 3}`). Threshold 3 encodes "a list, not a mention". This registry is itself governed: it lives next to the scripts and is code-owned by the architect.

Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 violations found, 2 internal error (must be distinguishable so CI fails closed rather than treating a crash as "clean").

Output format is a single line per violation: `GOV-00n <path>:<line> <detail>` plus a GitHub Actions `::error file=…,line=…::` annotation when `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.

## Test plan

- **Unit (pytest, `scripts/tests/`)**: clean fixture tree → exit 0; fixture with a dangling id → exit 1 + `GOV-002` with correct file:line; fixture with a duplicated list at/above threshold → exit 1 + `GOV-003`; fixture with a single mention below threshold → exit 0; allowlisted duplication → exit 0; unreadable file / bad encoding → exit 2 with a clear message and no traceback.
- **Integration**: run both scripts over the real repository in CI; asserted clean.
- **Contract/E2E/perf/chaos**: N/A.
- Coverage target: ≥85% line coverage on `scripts/` per `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #3 thresholds applied to Python.

## Security notes

Threat: tampering with governance text to weaken a guardrail without detection (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13 supply chain, integrity of the SDLC). Controls: `/CONSTITUTION.md` is code-owned by `@basiltt @CandleViewer/architecture @CandleViewer/security` in `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so any edit requires security review; the amendment process (C-16.1/C-16.2) adds a 3-working-day discussion period and entrenchment for scope guardrails and safety invariants. Scripts must not execute or eval file contents — they only read text. No secrets, PII or financial data touched. Security review label applied because this Task governs the integrity of every later security control.

## Accessibility notes

The constitution is a contributor-facing document. Verify during the sweep: one H1, correctly nested headings (the existing ToC anchors must still resolve), tables have header rows, and every mermaid diagram has an adjacent prose summary. Deeper verification of GitHub-rendered surfaces is E01-D02.

## Performance notes

Both scripts must complete in **≤5 s** over the full tree on the reference dev machine, keeping the governance job inside the ≤60 s epic budget. Measured and recorded in the PR.

## Observability

Stable `GOV-002` / `GOV-003` codes make failures greppable across CI history; GitHub annotations surface them inline on the PR diff. A `--json` output mode is provided so E01-Q02 can aggregate violation counts over time.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Repository sweep complete; before/after violation counts in the PR description; both checkers green on `main`.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met for `scripts/`.
- [ ] Docs: `AGENTS.md` §4 gains the command names (it is the sole owner of command names per C-16.5); no other doc restates them. ADR not required (no new architectural decision).
- [ ] Security: reviewed by the Security engineer; SAST clean on the new scripts.
- [ ] Demo: before/after checker output shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

No blockers. Blocks E01-T02, T03, T04, T05, T06, T08 and Q01 — every one of those either edits a governed document or must pass these checkers, so establishing the enforcement first prevents re-work.

## Branch

`feat/gov-constitution-ratify`. PR size: scripts + tests ~250 LOC; the reconciliation deletions may push the diff past 400 LOC — if so, split the sweep into a second `docs/gov-sot-dedup` PR.

## References

CandleViewer's situation is unusual and the document must reflect it accurately rather than copying a generic OSS policy: the repository is **private**, the deployment is **self-hosted for one owner plus a few managers**, reachable **only over Tailscale** (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.7, TB-1 in the trust-boundary diagram), and it handles **exchange API keys and live order flow** — so the realistic reporters are the internal team, contracted pen-testers (the R4 pen-test gate in `07-release-and-prr.md` §6), and dependency/security researchers reporting upstream CVEs, not anonymous internet finders.

- **Reporting channel**: a private route (GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting enabled on the repo, plus a named email/Signal fallback for when GitHub itself is the affected surface), with explicit instruction never to open a public issue and never to include a real API key or session cookie in a report.
- **Supported versions table**: which released versions receive fixes, tied to the release trains in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §1 (R0 `0.1.0` … GA). - **Severity guidance**: what counts as critical here — anything touching API-key confidentiality, the withdrawal-permission-always-off invariant, RBAC bypass, the fan-out native-SL invariant, or audit-log integrity.
- **In-scope / out-of-scope surfaces** for a report, consistent with `04-security-program.md` §1.3.
- **Safe-harbour statement** for good-faith testing by contracted testers, with the explicit prohibition on testing against the **live** environment (demo/staging only — mirrors the demo-not-prod rule in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- Cross-links out to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` for the full programme; `SECURITY.md` stays short and operational.

## Out of scope

- The security programme itself (threat models, SR-xxx requirements, RBAC matrix) — owned by `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, linked not restated.
- Implementing any control (key encryption, RBAC, audit hash-chaining) — E09, E27 and the security epics.
- Running the pen-test — R4 / E43.
- A bug-bounty programme — explicitly declined for a private self-hosted product; state that so it is a decision, not an omission.

```gherkin
  Given someone discovers a vulnerability in CandleViewer
  When they read SECURITY.md
  Then they find a single primary private reporting route and one fallback for when GitHub is the affected surface
  And they are told explicitly not to open a public issue and not to paste credentials into the report

Scenario: Severity drives a stated timeline
  Given a reported issue that would expose a Bybit API key
  When the severity is assessed against SECURITY.md
  Then it maps to P0 Critical with the acknowledgement, triage and fix-before commitments stated
  And those values match docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md section 11.3 without restating the whole table

Scenario: Live-environment testing is prohibited (failure path)
  Given a contracted tester plans to exercise the order path
  When they consult the safe-harbour section
  Then testing against the live environment is explicitly excluded from safe harbour
  And the demo environment is named as the only permitted target

Scenario: The document owns its content exclusively
  Given all tracked documents
  When scripts/check-sot-duplication.py runs
  Then vulnerability-reporting and supported-version content appears only in SECURITY.md
  And the check exits 0
```

## Technical notes / design

Enable **GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting** on the repository (Settings → Security) and reference the resulting advisory workflow; this gives a private fork for the fix and a CVE-less coordinated advisory, which suits a private repo. Document the escalation chain: reporter → Security engineer (triage) → Owner `@basiltt` (disposition) → fix ticket with `security` label → re-scan proof before close.

Supported-versions table format: `| Version | Supported | Notes |` with rows generated from the train table in `07-release-and-prr.md` §1; add a one-line rule ("only the latest tag on the current train receives fixes") so the table does not need editing at every patch release.

Severity mapping links to `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 by reference and adds only the CandleViewer-specific *examples* that belong to security (key exposure, withdrawal toggle, RBAC bypass, missing native SL, audit-chain break) — examples are not the owned list, so this is not a C-16.5 violation; confirm with the checker.

- **Process test (tabletop)**: run one dry-run report end to end — submit a fake advisory through the private channel, confirm it reaches the Security engineer, confirm the acknowledgement SLA is achievable, and confirm the fix ticket can be created with the `security` label without leaking details into a public surface. - **Negative test**: confirm a public issue containing the word "vulnerability" triggers the guidance path (a template hint in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` pointing at the private route) — implemented in E01-T05, verified here.

This Task *is* a security control: it determines whether a real finding reaches the right person privately and quickly. title: Make .github/CODEOWNERS cover every path and prove it with a checker
body:
## Context

R0 exit criterion #1 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires that "no path in the repo is un-owned by `CODEOWNERS`". `CONSTITUTION.md` C-8.1 states "A directory without an owner is a defect; add it to CODEOWNERS in the same PR that creates it", and C-10.1 requires at least one approval from a CODEOWNER of a touched directory — which silently degrades to "any two reviewers" for any path that matches only the default rule.

`.github/CODEOWNERS` exists (193 lines) with a sensible team structure and a catch-all `*  @basiltt @CandleViewer/architecture`. The catch-all means GitHub always finds *an* owner, so GitHub itself will never report a gap — the risk is invisible. What we actually need is the stronger property: every tracked path matches a **specific** rule chosen deliberately, not the fallback. Without a checker, E02's new packages (`chart-engine`, `protocol`, `ui`, `app-web`, `app-electron`, `services/api`) and every later directory will land owned-by-default, routing chart-engine reviews to the architect instead of `@CandleViewer/chart-engine`.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py`** — stdlib-only Python 3.12 implementing GitHub's CODEOWNERS matching semantics (gitignore-style patterns, later rules win, `/`-anchoring, directory patterns) and reporting, for every path from `git ls-files`: the winning rule and its owners. Fails with `GOV-001` for any path whose winning rule is the catch-all `*` (unless allowlisted), for any rule that matches nothing (dead rule — a strong signal of a typo or a moved directory), and for any owner not in the declared team list at the top of the file.
- **`scripts/codeowners-allowlist.txt`** — explicit, justified exceptions (e.g. `LICENSE`), each line requiring a `# reason:` comment; the checker rejects an entry without one.
- **CODEOWNERS updated** so every currently tracked path has a deliberate rule, and forward-looking rules are added for the E02 package layout (`/packages/chart-engine/`, `/packages/protocol/`, `/packages/ui/`, `/packages/fixtures/`, `/apps/web/`, `/apps/electron/`, `/services/api/`, `/docs/plan/backlog/`, `/scripts/`) so those directories are owned the moment they are created rather than a PR later.
- **Dead-rule cleanup** — remove or fix rules pointing at paths that do not and will not exist.
- A short ownership-rationale comment block per section (already the file's style) kept accurate.

## Out of scope

- Creating the GitHub teams themselves (org administration; the placeholders `@CandleViewer/*` are documented in the file header and provisioned by the Owner — a checklist item on this ticket, not a code change).
- Branch protection's "require review from Code Owners" toggle — E01-T08.
- Ownership of directories that E02 will restructure: rules are added speculatively here and **verified** by re-running this checker as part of E02's DoD (recorded as a checklist item on E02).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every tracked path has a deliberate owner
  Given the repository at this branch head
  When scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py runs
  Then it exits 0
  And it reports 0 paths falling through to the catch-all rule outside the allowlist

Scenario: A new un-owned directory is caught
  Given a new directory services/newthing/main.py is added with no CODEOWNERS rule
  When scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py runs
  Then it prints GOV-001 naming services/newthing/main.py and the catch-all rule that matched it
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: A dead rule is caught
  Given CODEOWNERS contains a rule for /packages/typo-name/ which matches no tracked path
  When the checker runs with dead-rule detection enabled
  Then it reports the dead rule with its line number
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: Matching semantics agree with GitHub (later rules win)
  Given CODEOWNERS contains a general /docs/ rule followed by a specific /docs/plan/backlog/ rule
  When the checker resolves owners for docs/plan/backlog/E01.json
  Then the owners reported are those of the specific later rule, not the general earlier one
```

## Technical notes / design

Matching semantics to implement (validated against GitHub's documented behaviour and spot-checked against the real repo's "Owners" UI for three sample paths): patterns are gitignore-like; the **last** matching pattern wins; a pattern with no leading `/` matches at any depth; a trailing `/` matches a directory and everything under it; `*` does not cross `/` but `**` does. Implement with `fnmatch`-based segment matching rather than a regex soup, and unit-test each rule class.

The dead-rule check needs care with the forward-looking E02 rules: those legitimately match nothing today. Solve with a `# future:` marker comment on such rules — the checker skips dead-rule reporting for marked rules but emits a warning summary listing them, and E02's DoD requires removing the markers once the directories exist. This keeps "planned" distinct from "typo" without weakening the check.

Output: `GOV-001 <path> matched-by:<line> owners:<catch-all>` plus GitHub annotations. Exit codes 0/1/2 as established in E01-T01 (2 = internal error, so CI fails closed).

## Test plan

- **Unit (pytest)**: a fixture CODEOWNERS + fixture path list exercising each matching rule class (depth-free pattern, anchored pattern, directory pattern, `**`, later-wins override, owner-not-in-team-list, allowlist entry without a reason → error, `# future:` marked rule); catch-all fallthrough detection; dead-rule detection; unreadable file → exit 2.
- **Integration**: run over the real repository in CI, asserted clean; plus a "canary" test that creates a temporary un-owned path in a scratch checkout and asserts non-zero exit.
- **Manual cross-check**: for three representative paths (`CONSTITUTION.md`, `.github/workflows/x.yml`, `docs/plan/backlog/E01.json`) compare the checker's computed owners against GitHub's own CODEOWNERS resolution shown in the PR UI; discrepancies are bugs in the checker, not in GitHub.
- Coverage target: ≥85% line coverage on `scripts/`.

## Security notes

Ownership is an access-control mechanism: it decides who must approve a change to `/services/api/`, `/.github/workflows/`, key handling, and the constitution itself (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13 supply chain). Threats: (E) privilege escalation by landing a sensitive change through a path with only default ownership, so no security reviewer is pulled in; (T) tampering with CODEOWNERS itself — mitigated because `/.github/CODEOWNERS` is code-owned by `@basiltt @CandleViewer/architecture`, so weakening it requires their approval; (R) repudiation — the file's git history is the audit trail. Additional control from this Task: the owner-not-in-declared-team-list check catches a typo'd or attacker-inserted owner handle, which would otherwise silently satisfy "a code-owner approved". Security-engineer review required. No secrets, PII or financial data.

## Accessibility notes

N/A — no user interface. The CODEOWNERS header comment block remains plain text and readable without colour.

## Performance notes

Checker must complete in **≤5 s** over the full tracked file list on the reference machine (it is O(paths × rules); memoise per-directory results to stay linear in practice). Measured and recorded in the PR, keeping the governance job under the 60 s epic budget.

## Observability

`GOV-001` codes and GitHub annotations on the PR diff. A `--report` mode prints an ownership table (path glob → owners) that E01-Q02 archives as a CI artefact, giving a diffable history of how ownership changed over the project's life — useful evidence at the R4 live-enablement gate.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests, incl. the canary un-owned-path test.
- [ ] Real repository clean; ownership report artefact produced.
- [ ] GitHub teams `@CandleViewer/*` confirmed to exist (or the placeholder status explicitly recorded with a dated follow-up owned by `@basiltt`).
- [ ] Coverage threshold met for `scripts/`.
- [ ] Docs: `AGENTS.md` §4 gains the command name; forward-looking rules and their `# future:` markers noted as an E02 DoD checklist item.
- [ ] Security: reviewed by the Security engineer (ownership is an access control).
- [ ] Demo: show a deliberately un-owned path failing CI.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

`blocked_by: E01-T01` (shares the script conventions, exit codes, `GOV-00n` output contract and test harness established there). Blocks `E01-T08` — branch protection's code-owner requirement is only meaningful once ownership is total.

`feat/gov-codeowners-coverage`. PR size: ~250 LOC script + tests plus CODEOWNERS edits; within guidance.

title: Refresh PR template and issue forms to the ticket taxonomy
body:
## Context

The repository ships `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (135 lines) and four issue forms (`epic.yml`, `feature_request.yml`, `bug_report.yml`, `config.yml`). They predate the locked taxonomy in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5: six Kinds (Epic, Story, Task, Spike, Bug, Chore), one `area/*` label from a closed list of 17, one `priority/*` from four, and eight cross-cutting labels (`design`, `ux-research`, `design-qa`, `handoff`, `security`, `a11y`, `perf`, `qa`) each of which "triggers a required workflow step".

The templates are the data-entry layer for every gate the rest of this epic automates: the board automation in E01-T07 can only check "is there a QA sign-off" if the form creates a stable, machine-findable place for it; the `pr-metadata` required check (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #20) validates "`Closes #N` present, branch-name pattern, diff-size policy, changed-files vs labels sanity" — all of which depend on template structure. `CONSTITUTION.md` C-16.5 names `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` as the **sole owner of PR-checklist wording**, so this file must not restate the required-check table or the DoD lists; it links.

The information architecture and field set for the forms are designed in **E01-D01** (this ticket implements that design — hence the `handoff` label and the D01 dependency).

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`** rewritten per the D01 spec: what/why, linked ticket (`Closes #N`), Kind/area/priority confirmation, test evidence, screenshots/recording for UI changes, risk note, the self-check list from `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` expressed as a short checklist that **links** to the DoD rather than copying it, and a "why this can't be split" field that appears only when the diff exceeds 400 LOC (documented instruction, enforced by `pr-metadata`).
- **Issue forms** — one per Kind, replacing the current generic set: `epic.yml`, `story.yml`, `task.yml`, `spike.yml`, `bug_report.yml`, `chore.yml`. Each form collects exactly the fields its DoR requires (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §§2–7): e.g. Story requires Gherkin acceptance criteria, test-plan outline, design-link, estimate; Spike requires question, timebox, decision criteria; Bug requires repro steps, expected vs actual, severity, regression-gap note.
- **Structured, machine-findable sections** — each gate-relevant field emitted under a stable heading (`### QA sign-off`, `### Security review`, `### a11y evidence`) so E01-T07's guards can parse the issue body deterministically; the exact contract is documented in a short comment block and referenced by T07.
- **Dropdowns for the closed vocabularies** — Kind, `area/*` (all 17), `priority/*` (all 4), Component, Perspective, Risk (R1–R15/None), Estimate (1/2/3/5/8) — matching the board field schema in `00-planning-brief.md` and the ticket schema from E01-T06.
- **`config.yml`** — `blank_issues_enabled: false`, plus contact links: security reports routed to the private channel in `SECURITY.md` (never a public issue), and a "question" link to Discussions.
- **Default labels applied by each form** (`labels:` key) so Kind↔label sync in T07 starts from a correct state.

## Out of scope

- The automation that reads these fields — E01-T07.
- The `pr-metadata` CI job implementation — E03 (this ticket only guarantees the template structure it parses, and documents the contract).
- Designing the IA/field set — E01-D01 (same sprint, design-first under the recorded Architect/CDO design-ahead waiver in this ticket; this ticket implements that spec and does not invent it).
- Creating the GitHub labels themselves — a one-time repo-admin action tracked as a checklist item here, scripted in `scripts/sync-labels.py` if E01-K01 shows the API path is trivial.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: A Story cannot be filed without its DoR fields
  Given the story issue form
  When a user submits it without acceptance criteria
  Then GitHub blocks submission because the field is marked required
  And the rendered issue contains a stable "### Acceptance criteria" heading when submitted correctly

Scenario: Gate sections are machine-parsable
  Given an issue created from the story form
  When the board automation parses the issue body for the QA sign-off section
  Then it locates the section by its stable heading without heuristics
  And a missing section is distinguishable from an empty one

Scenario: Closed vocabularies cannot be freetyped
  Given the task issue form
  When a user selects an area
  Then only the 17 area values from docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md section 5.2 are offered
  And no free-text alternative for that field exists

Scenario: Security reports are diverted from public issues (failure path)
  Given a user clicks "New issue" intending to report a vulnerability
  When the chooser renders
  Then blank issues are disabled and a contact link points to the private route defined in SECURITY.md
  And no issue form invites vulnerability details

Scenario: The PR template duplicates no owned list
  Given .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md at this branch head
  When scripts/check-sot-duplication.py runs
  Then it exits 0 and the template links to CONSTITUTION.md section 9 rather than restating check names
```

## Design-ahead waiver (Architect/CDO) — explicit record

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires a linked design artefact to have been **Done for ≥2 sprints** before the consuming ticket starts, *or* an explicit Architect/CDO waiver recorded with a reason. This chain — `E01-D01` (design, Sprint 01) → `E01-T05` (build, Sprint 01) → `E01-D02` (design-QA, Sprint 02) — runs at a 0–1 sprint gap, so the waiver path applies and is recorded here explicitly rather than left implicit in the Kind=Task classification.

- **Waiver granted by:** Architect (repo/architecture owner) and CDO, at Sprint 01 planning; both countersign as a ticket comment before this ticket leaves Ready.
- **Scope of waiver:** the E01 contributor surface only — `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and the rendered governance markdown. It does **not** extend to any `SCR-*` product screen; every customer-facing screen from E05 onward observes the full 2-sprint rule with no exception.
- **Reasons (all four hold):**
  1. **No Sprint −1 exists.** E01 is the first ticket set of the first sprint of the programme; a 2-sprint lead time is arithmetically unavailable and no sequencing creates it.
  2. **Contributor-facing, not customer-facing.** The audience is the delivery team plus reviewers. Iteration cost is one PR against a YAML file, the feedback loop is hours rather than a release train, and there is no migration, no stored user state and no public commitment to the layout.
  3. **No design-system dependency.** These surfaces are rendered by GitHub's own chrome — the design freedom is information architecture, field set, wording and required flags, none of which consume the design-system v0 tokens delivered in E05. There is no risk of designing against an unbuilt foundation, which is the risk the 2-sprint rule exists to prevent.
  4. **Blocking cost is programme-wide.** Deferring the forms to Sprint 03 means every ticket filed in Sprints 01–02 across E01–E10 is captured without the DoR fields the board automation parses, producing a backlog that must be retro-fitted by hand.
- **Compensating controls (the waiver is not a free pass):**
  - Design lands **first within Sprint 01** — `E01-D01` must be Status=Done before `E01-T05` opens a PR; `blocked_by` enforces the ordering even though the sprint is shared.
  - A **mid-sprint 30-minute design/engineering walkthrough** of the field set replaces the missing soak time; deltas are amended into the D01 spec, not absorbed silently in the build.
  - The **full design-QA and a11y pass still happens** (`E01-D02`, Sprint 02) and the epic cannot reach Done without it — verification is deferred by one sprint, never skipped.
  - Any discrepancy found in D02 is fixed or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*`, so the shortened lead time surfaces as tracked defects rather than silent quality loss.
- **Expiry:** this waiver covers E01 only and sets no precedent. If a second Sprint-01-style exception is requested in R0, the Architect raises it at the R0 retro as a proposed standing amendment to `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1 instead of granting waivers case-by-case.

## Technical notes / design

GitHub issue **forms** (YAML) are used rather than markdown templates, because forms give required-field validation, closed dropdowns, and a predictable rendered body — all prerequisites for reliable parsing. Each `textarea`/`dropdown` gets an `id` matching its rendered heading slug so parsing can key on either.

Rendered-body contract (documented at the top of each form and duplicated nowhere else): headings are `### <Label>` exactly as written in the form's `label:`; an unanswered optional field renders as `_No response_`, which the T07 guards must treat as "absent" — this specific string is the contract and is asserted by a test.

The PR template keeps a hard ceiling of ~60 lines of checklist: a template nobody reads is a control that does not exist. Depth lives behind links to `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` and `CONSTITUTION.md` §9.

Labels declared per form: `epic.yml → type/epic`, `story.yml → type/story`, etc., matching §5.2 so T07's Kind↔label sync is idempotent on creation.

## Test plan

- **Unit/contract**: a schema test validating every `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` against GitHub's issue-forms schema (catches the silent-breakage class where a malformed form disappears from the chooser); a parser test asserting that a rendered body from each form yields every gate section, including the `_No response_` case.
- **Integration**: create one issue from each form on a scratch repo; assert default labels applied and body parses.
- **E2E (manual)**: file one real issue per Kind and one real PR using the template; confirm the flow is not annoying enough to invite bypass — recorded under E01-Q01's exploratory charter.
- **a11y**: axe-equivalent manual checks per E01-D02 (forms are GitHub-rendered, so the control we have is field labelling and description quality).
- Coverage: parser/validator code lives in `scripts/` and carries the ≥85% threshold.

## Security notes

Threats: (I) information disclosure — a well-meaning reporter pastes an API key, session cookie or account id into a public issue; mitigated by disabling blank issues, routing security to the private channel from `SECURITY.md`, and adding an explicit "never paste credentials, keys, or real account identifiers" warning in every form's description. (T) Template tampering to remove a gate section, silently disabling a T07 guard; mitigated by CODEOWNERS on `/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and by T07 failing closed when a section is missing rather than passing. (S) Spoofing a sign-off by typing "QA: approved" into the body rather than obtaining a real reviewer comment — explicitly addressed by T07 requiring an *actor-attributed* comment, not body text; the template must therefore not present the sign-off as something the author fills in. Data classification: public-internal metadata. Security review required on the diverting/config behaviour.

## Accessibility notes

Owned surface, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: every form field has a real `label` (never placeholder-as-label); `description` text gives the constraint in words, not colour or emoji; required fields are marked with `validations: required: true` so they are announced programmatically rather than by a visual asterisk; dropdown option text is self-describing out of context (`priority/p0-critical — drop everything` rather than `p0`); the PR template uses proper heading nesting and header-row tables; no information conveyed by emoji alone. Audited and signed off in **E01-D02**.

## Performance notes

N/A at runtime. Process budget: filing a Task must take under 2 minutes; anything longer causes contributors to route around the forms, which destroys the data the automation depends on. Validated during the E01-Q01 exploratory session.

## Observability

The stable heading contract is what makes every later gate decision auditable; T07 logs which section it parsed and what it found. Track (from R0) the rate of issues created outside the forms (should be zero once blank issues are disabled) as a drift indicator.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified; one issue per Kind filed on the scratch repo as evidence.
- [ ] Forms validate against GitHub's issue-forms schema in CI; parser contract test green incl. the `_No response_` case.
- [ ] `check-sot-duplication.py` and `check-rule-refs.sh` green on the template and forms.

title: Publish the backlog ticket JSON schema and validate every backlog file
body:
## Context

`CONSTITUTION.md` C-16.5 names **`docs/plan/backlog/schema/`** as the sole owner of the "Ticket schema". `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §29 requires the planning phase to deliver `docs/plan/backlog/*.json` as "full ticket tree … with every field required by the project schema", and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 requires each story's test plan to live *inside* the backlog ticket so it travels with the ticket.

Today the schema is referenced but does not exist. Roughly fifty epic files (E01…E49) are being authored in parallel against a prose description of the field set; without a machine-checkable schema, drift is guaranteed — a missing `perspective`, a `risk` value outside R1–R15, an `estimate` of 13 that should have been split, a `blocked_by` pointing at a ticket key that was never created. Each of those becomes a broken import into the GitHub Project and a manual reconciliation.

This Task publishes the schema and the validator, and makes them a required gate on the backlog directory.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`docs/plan/backlog/schema/ticket.schema.json`** — JSON Schema (2020-12) for a single ticket object: required keys `key`, `kind`, `title`, `labels`, `component`, `phase`, `sprint`, `priority`, `perspective`, `risk`, `estimate`, `parent`, `blocked_by`, `milestone`, `body`; closed enums for `kind`, `component`, `phase`, `priority`, `perspective`, `risk`, `milestone`, `sprint`, and `estimate` (1|2|3|5|8, with 13 permitted only when `kind == "Epic"`); `key` pattern `^E\d{2}(-[STKDQX]\d{2})?$`; `title` `maxLength: 80`; `labels` requiring exactly one `type/*`, one `area/*`, one `priority/*` from the closed lists in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2.
- **`docs/plan/backlog/schema/backlog-file.schema.json`** — the array form: first element must be the epic (`kind: "Epic"`, `parent: null`), all other elements must have `parent` equal to the epic key or to a sibling key in the same file.
- **`docs/plan/backlog/schema/README.md`** — field-by-field semantics, the key-prefix convention (S Story, T Task, K Spike, D Design, Q QA, X Security), and the rule that this directory is the single source of truth for the schema (C-16.5).
- **`scripts/validate-backlog.py`** — validates every `docs/plan/backlog/*.json` against the schemas **plus** cross-file semantic rules a JSON Schema cannot express:
  - `blocked_by` entries resolve to a real key in this file, a real key in another backlog file, or a bare epic id `E\d{2}` present in `docs/plan/backlog_epics_seed.json`;
  - no dependency cycles (report the cycle path);
  - `parent` chains terminate at the epic;
  - the epic's `estimate` equals the sum of its children's estimates (warning if outside ±15% of the roadmap's budgeted `pts` for that epic, read from `backlog_epics_seed.json`);
  - `sprint` respects `blocked_by` ordering (a ticket may not be scheduled before a ticket that blocks it) and lies inside the epic's train window as given by `30-release-roadmap.md` §3;
  - design tickets (`key` prefix `D`) are scheduled at least 2 sprints before any ticket that lists them in `blocked_by` — the design-ahead rule from `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1;
  - `body` contains every heading of the mandated body template.
  Emits `GOV-004` per violation, exit codes 0/1/2 as established in E01-T01.
- CI wiring stub so E01-Q02 can add it to the `governance` job.

## Out of scope

- Authoring the ticket content itself (each epic's planner does that).
- The importer that pushes tickets into GitHub Projects (a follow-up filed by E01-K01 if the spike shows it is needed).
- The GitHub Project field configuration — E01-T07 / repo admin.
- Changing the agreed field set: if a field is genuinely missing, it is raised with the Architect and, if it touches C-16.5, amended per C-16.1.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every existing backlog file validates
  Given all files matching docs/plan/backlog/*.json
  When scripts/validate-backlog.py runs
  Then it exits 0 and reports zero GOV-004 violations

Scenario: A missing required field is rejected with a precise pointer
  Given a ticket object with no "perspective" key
  When the validator runs
  Then it prints GOV-004 with the file, the ticket key, and the JSON pointer to the offending object
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: A dangling dependency is rejected
  Given a ticket whose blocked_by lists E99-S42 which exists in no backlog file and no epic seed
  When the validator runs
  Then it reports the unresolvable dependency and exits non-zero

Scenario: A dependency cycle is reported with its path
  Given E01-T04 blocked_by E01-T08 and E01-T08 blocked_by E01-T04
  When the validator runs
  Then it prints the cycle path E01-T04 -> E01-T08 -> E01-T04
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: The design-ahead rule is enforced
  Given a frontend Story in Sprint 05 whose blocked_by includes a design ticket scheduled in Sprint 04
  When the validator runs
  Then it reports a design-ahead violation naming both tickets and the required 2-sprint gap
  And it exits non-zero

Scenario: An oversized story is rejected
  Given a ticket with kind Story and estimate 13
  When the validator runs
  Then it is rejected because estimates above 8 require a split for non-Epic kinds
```

## Technical notes / design

Schema draft 2020-12, validated with `jsonschema` — the one third-party dependency permitted here; if E02's Python environment is not yet available, vendor a minimal validator path and note the follow-up to switch to `jsonschema` once `uv` exists (recorded as an E02 checklist item). Prefer `jsonschema` if installable, since hand-rolling draft-2020-12 is not worth the maintenance.

Enums are **generated**, not hand-copied: `scripts/validate-backlog.py` derives the `area/*` and `priority/*` lists by parsing `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2, and the sprint/train windows by parsing `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3. This is deliberate — hand-copied enums are exactly the C-16.5 duplication failure mode. If parsing proves brittle, fall back to a generated-and-committed `enums.json` with a `generated-code-check` (CI §9 #19) asserting it is up to date.

Sprint-ordering rule: map `Sprint NN` → integer, `Backlog` → +∞; for each edge `a blocked_by b`, require `sprint(b) <= sprint(a)`, and for design edges require `sprint(b) + 2 <= sprint(a)`. Cross-epic edges pointing at a bare epic id resolve to that epic's last-scheduled child; if the target epic file does not exist yet, the check is deferred with a warning rather than a failure, so epics can land in any order during the planning phase — and E01-Q02's nightly run turns those warnings into failures once all files exist.

## Test plan

- **Unit (pytest)**: one case per rule above, each with a minimal invalid fixture and the expected message; plus a valid golden ticket; plus malformed JSON → exit 2 with the parse position.
- **Contract**: the golden valid ticket is also used by E01-T07 as the shape it imports, so it is a shared fixture — a change to the schema that breaks it fails both.
- **Integration**: run over the whole real `docs/plan/backlog/` tree in CI (this is the gate that keeps ~50 parallel epic files coherent).
- **Regression**: the deferred-cross-epic-warning behaviour is tested both ways (target absent → warn; target present but mis-ordered → fail).
- Coverage target: ≥85% on `scripts/`.

## Security notes

Threats: (T) the validator is the only thing standing between a malformed/hostile backlog file and an automated importer that will create issues with that content — so the validator must treat ticket `body` as **data, never as instructions or a template to execute**; no `eval`, no Jinja rendering of ticket content, no shell interpolation of any field. (I) Ticket bodies are authored by humans and agents and could contain a pasted secret; add a cheap secret-pattern scan over ticket bodies (reusing the repo's gitleaks rules if available) and fail on a hit — a backlog file is a tracked file and inherits `secrets-scan` (CI §9 #12) anyway, but failing early with a `GOV-004` gives a clearer message. Data classification: public-internal planning metadata. No PII, no financial data, no credentials.

## Accessibility notes

N/A — no user interface. The schema README follows the same markdown a11y conventions (single H1, nested headings, header-row tables).

## Performance notes

Validating ~50 files with ~20 tickets each (~1000 objects, several MB of markdown bodies) must complete in **≤10 s**; avoid re-parsing the plan docs per file by caching the derived enums once per run. Measured and recorded.

## Observability

`GOV-004` codes plus JSON pointers; GitHub annotations at file/line where derivable. A `--summary` mode prints per-epic ticket counts, point totals and the delta versus the roadmap's budgeted `pts`, archived as a CI artefact — this becomes the planning phase's own progress dashboard and directly supports the epic-budget reconciliation the roadmap requires.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Schemas and README published under `docs/plan/backlog/schema/`; C-16.5 registry row is satisfied (no other file restates the ticket schema — checker green).
- [ ] All acceptance criteria covered by automated tests; validator green over the real backlog tree.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met for `scripts/`.
- [ ] Docs: `AGENTS.md` §4 command entry added; `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1's `test_plan` expectation reconciled with the actual body-template section ("## Test plan") so the two documents agree.
- [ ] QA sign-off: QA validates that a story's test plan is recoverable from the ticket body alone.
- [ ] Demo: `--summary` output shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T01` (script conventions, `GOV-00n` contract, and the C-16.5 duplication checker that enforces this directory's exclusive ownership). Blocks `E01-T07` (the importer/automation consumes this schema) and `E01-Q02` (the regression pack runs this validator). Every other epic's backlog file depends on this schema existing, which is why it is Sprint 01.
