title: Implement board automation: Kind-label sync and QA/security/a11y close guards
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2 commits to specific automation: "a Story/Bug cannot move to Done without `qa` sign-off recorded (a bot comment or a required 'QA Sign-off' checkbox in the issue body); a ticket labelled `security` cannot close without a comment from a Security-team member; `a11y`-labelled tickets require a linked axe-core CI run URL." `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 lists the same four automations as E01 scope: label↔Kind sync, QA-sign-off bot, security-close guard, a11y run-link guard.

These are not conveniences — they are the enforcement layer for `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`. §8 of that document is explicit that "QA sign-off for Story/Bug is never silently skipped" and that security-labelled tickets are "always treated as `security`-labelled for DoD purposes, whether or not the label was applied at creation". Human discipline across ~15 engineers and a large design org over 26 sprints will not hold that line unaided.

The design constraints (credential, event availability, whether a close can be *blocked* or only *compensated*) are decided by **E01-K01** and recorded in ADR-0016; this Task implements whatever that ADR concluded.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`.github/workflows/board-automation.yml`** with four jobs, each independently testable:
  1. **Kind↔label sync** — on issue `opened`/`edited`/`labeled`/`unlabeled` and on project-item field change (if observable per ADR-0016): keep the `type/*` label and the board `Kind` field in agreement, using the issue-form default as the seed. Idempotent; never fights a human edit twice (loop guard: skip if the last change was made by this workflow's own actor).
  2. **QA-sign-off guard** — on issue `closed` where Kind ∈ {Story, Bug}: require an actor-attributed sign-off, i.e. a comment from a member of `@CandleViewer/qa` matching a documented marker (`QA sign-off: pass`), **or** an explicitly recorded "QA capacity deviation" statement by the ticket owner (permitted by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). Absent that, reopen (or block, per ADR-0016) and post a comment naming the missing DoD item with a link to §3.2.
  3. **Security-close guard** — on issue `closed` where the ticket carries `security`, **or** touches the always-security paths listed in §8 (`area/auth-rbac`, `area/oms-execution`, API-key handling, withdrawal settings, fan-out SL): require a comment from a `@CandleViewer/security` member. Additionally, on `labeled`/`opened`, auto-apply the `security` label when an always-security `area/*` is present, so the label cannot be omitted at creation.
  4. **a11y run-link guard** — on issue `closed` where the ticket carries `a11y`: require a linked axe-core CI run URL in the body's `### a11y evidence` section or in a comment, validated as a URL pointing at this repository's Actions runs (not an arbitrary link).
- **Shared parsing module** (`scripts/gh/issue_body.py`) implementing the rendered-body contract from E01-T05 (stable `### Heading` sections, `_No response_` = absent), unit-tested independently of GitHub.
- **Fail-closed behaviour**: any API error, rate limit or unexpected state results in the guard blocking (or reopening) with an explicit "guard could not verify" comment — never a silent pass.
- **Audit comments**: every gate decision posts exactly one comment recording allowed/blocked, which rule, and which DoD item; repeat evaluations edit the existing comment rather than spamming.
- **Credential** provisioned per ADR-0016 (GitHub App installation token preferred), stored as an Actions secret, with the rotation owner recorded.
- **Dry-run mode** (`GOVERNANCE_ENFORCE=false` repo variable) so the guards can run in observe-only mode for the first sprint, logging what they *would* have blocked — then flipped to enforcing with evidence that the false-positive rate is zero.

## Out of scope

- Blocking *merges* — that is branch protection, E01-T08.
- Any Projects v2 field beyond `Kind` (Sprint/Phase/Estimate population is manual or handled by the importer follow-up from E01-K01).
- The bulk backlog import.
- The `pr-metadata` CI job (E03).

**Security-control linkage (added per PR #1411 review, AC3):** this ticket is the owning delivery for SR-162 (QA-sign-off guard: sign-off MUST be a structured, audit-logged reviewer action, never free text - `04-security-program.md` §6.17), SR-165 (`pull_request_target` grep-based CI check, §6.17 / G16), and SR-164 for the guard workflows themselves (least-privilege `permissions:` blocks, §6.17 / G12, G18). The acceptance criteria above (QA-sign-off guard, forged-sign-off rejection scenarios) already encode SR-162 and SR-165's behaviour; this note makes the SR <-> ticket traceability explicit so `04-security-program.md` §6.17 does not cite an orphaned requirement.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: A Story cannot be closed without QA sign-off
  Given an issue with Kind Story and no comment from a QA team member matching the sign-off marker
  When a maintainer closes the issue
  Then the guard reopens it (or blocks the close, per ADR-0016)
  And it posts one comment naming the missing DoD item from docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md section 3.2

Scenario: A recorded QA capacity deviation is accepted
  Given an issue with Kind Story whose owner has posted the documented QA capacity deviation statement
  When the issue is closed
  Then the guard allows the close
  And it posts an audit comment recording that the deviation path was used

Scenario: The security label cannot be omitted for an always-security area
  Given a new issue labelled area/auth-rbac without the security label
  When the issue is opened
  Then the automation adds the security label
  And a subsequent close without a comment from a security team member is blocked

Scenario: A forged sign-off in the body does not satisfy the guard (failure path)
  Given a Story whose author typed "QA sign-off: pass" into the issue body themselves
  When the issue is closed
  Then the guard does not accept it, because the marker must come from an actor-attributed comment by a QA team member
  And the close is blocked or reopened

Scenario: The guard fails closed on an API error
  Given the GitHub API returns 5xx while the guard checks team membership
  When the guard runs on a close event
  Then it does not allow the close
  And it posts a comment stating the gate could not be verified and must be re-run

Scenario: An a11y ticket requires a real run link
  Given an issue labelled a11y whose a11y evidence section contains a link to an external website
  When the issue is closed
  Then the guard rejects it because the link does not point at this repository's Actions runs
```

## Technical notes / design

Structure: a thin workflow YAML per event, delegating to Python in `scripts/gh/` so the logic is unit-testable without GitHub. Each guard is a pure function `evaluate(issue, comments, teams) -> Decision(allow|block, reason, dod_ref)`; the GitHub side-effects (reopen, comment, label) live in a separate thin adapter. This split is what makes the acceptance criteria testable offline.

Team membership is resolved via the API and **cached per run only** — never hard-coded, so adding a QA engineer does not require a workflow edit. A membership lookup failure is a fail-closed condition.

Loop guard: the workflow ignores events whose actor is its own app/bot identity; additionally each automation write is tagged with an HTML comment marker (`<!-- gov-bot:qa-guard -->`) so subsequent runs can find and edit their own prior comment.

Idempotency: all four jobs are safe to re-run on the same event; running them twice produces the same labels and exactly one audit comment.

Pinning: all third-party actions pinned to a full commit SHA (supply-chain control, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13). `permissions:` declared minimally per job (`issues: write`, `contents: read`; nothing else).

Rollout: ship with `GOVERNANCE_ENFORCE=false`, observe for the remainder of Sprint 01, review the would-have-blocked log at the sprint retro, then flip to `true` — recorded as a checklist item on this ticket, not a separate ticket, since the epic cannot be Done in observe-only mode.

## Test plan

- **Unit (pytest, ≥85% coverage)**: `evaluate()` for each guard across the matrix — sign-off present/absent, comment author in/out of team, deviation statement present, body-forged marker, `_No response_` section, missing section entirely, a11y link valid/foreign/absent, always-security area with and without the label, API-error injection → block.
- **Integration**: against a scratch repository (or `act` with a mocked API per ADR-0016), exercise each end-to-end path including the reopen-and-comment compensation and the idempotent re-run.
- **Contract**: the issue-body parser is tested against real rendered bodies produced by each E01-T05 form — a form change that breaks parsing fails here, which is the whole point of the shared fixture.
- **Chaos**: simulate rate-limit (403 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`) and partial-failure (comment posted, reopen fails) and assert the guard's state is recoverable on re-run.
- **E2E (manual)**: one real non-compliant issue per guard on the real repo before enforcement is switched on; screenshots attached.

## Security notes

This Task is itself a privileged automation and is the highest-risk item in E01 (see the STRIDE model in E01-X01 and the token review in E01-X02). Threats and controls:
- **(E) Privilege escalation via workflow token** — jobs declare least-privilege `permissions:`; no `write-all`; the credential (App installation token per ADR-0016) is repository-scoped; secrets are never exposed to fork-triggered events.
- **(E/T) Pwn-request** — `pull_request_target` is not used; guards trigger only on `issues`/`issue_comment` events, which do not check out untrusted code. No step executes content from an issue body; issue content is treated strictly as data (no shell interpolation — pass via environment variables or files, never inline into `run:`).
- **(S) Spoofed sign-off** — satisfied only by an actor-attributed comment from a verified team member, never by body text; this is an explicit acceptance criterion.
- **(T) Guard bypass by disabling the workflow** — `/.github/workflows/` is code-owned by `@CandleViewer/devsecops @CandleViewer/security`; the weekly `governance-drift` job (epic-level) alerts if the workflow is disabled.
- **(D) Denial** — fail-closed means an outage blocks closes rather than allowing them; accepted deliberately, with the manual override path being a documented, audited admin action.
- **(R) Repudiation** — every decision is an audit comment, permanently attached to the issue.
Data classification: public-internal metadata; the workflow must never echo the token or full API responses into logs. Security-engineer review and sign-off required before enforcement is enabled.

## Accessibility notes

The automation's user-visible output is its comments: they must be readable as plain text, use real headings and lists rather than ASCII art, never rely on emoji or colour alone to signal pass/fail (write "BLOCKED" / "ALLOWED" as words), and always include the actionable next step in prose. Per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4 colour-independence. Reviewed in E01-D02.

## Performance notes

Each guard must reach a decision within **30 s** of the triggering event so a maintainer is not left wondering whether the close succeeded; the compensating reopen (if that is the chosen control type) must land inside the 60 s ceiling recorded in ADR-0016, otherwise the gate design is revisited. Measured over the observe-only period and recorded.

## Observability

- One audit comment per decision (the primary, permanent record).
- Structured workflow logs: `GOV-006 <issue> <guard> <decision> <reason>`.
- Observe-only mode writes a would-have-blocked summary consumed at the retro.
- Weekly `governance-drift` run verifies the workflow is enabled and the credential is valid, opening a `priority/p1-high` issue otherwise.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by unit + integration tests; manual E2E evidence attached for each guard.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on `scripts/gh/`.
- [ ] Observe-only period completed with a zero false-positive result, then `GOVERNANCE_ENFORCE=true`.

- [ ] a11y: comment output checked against E01-D02's checklist.
- [ ] QA sign-off: QA executes the guard test plan from E01-Q01, including the forged-sign-off and fail-closed cases.
- [ ] Demo: a non-compliant close shown being blocked at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner (`/.github/workflows/` → devsecops + security).

title: Configure branch protection and merge queue as reviewable code
body:
## Context

R0 exit criterion #1 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires that "a PR without 2 approvals incl. a code-owner is demonstrably unmergeable". `CONSTITUTION.md` C-10.1 mandates 2 approvals with at least 1 CODEOWNER; §9 lists 20 exactly-named required checks and states "A red check is never merged; there is no 'admin merge'"; `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §6.1 requires protected `main` with linear history (squash/rebase only) and required conversation resolution, and §7 requires the GitHub **merge queue** with rebase-and-recheck before merge.

Today none of this is applied, and if it were applied by hand it would be invisible, undiffable and silently mutable. This Task makes the protection configuration a reviewed artefact in the repository, applies it idempotently, and adds drift detection — because an unnoticed protection rollback is indistinguishable from having no protection at all.

The required-check names are forward references: most of the 20 jobs are created by **E03**. GitHub treats a required check that never reports as "pending", which blocks merges — desirable as an end state, fatal on day 1 when no pipeline exists. The rollout below handles that explicitly.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`.github/branch-protection.json`** — the desired state for `main`: required approving reviews = 2, require review from Code Owners = true, dismiss stale approvals on push = true, require conversation resolution = true, require linear history = true, allow force pushes = false, allow deletions = false, enforce for administrators = true (no admin merge, per C-9.1), required status checks with `strict` rebase behaviour, and the merge-queue configuration (squash merge, rebase-and-recheck).
- **`scripts/apply-branch-protection.py`** — idempotent apply from that file via the REST API; `--dry-run` prints the diff between live and desired without changing anything; refuses to run if the desired file itself fails validation.
- **`scripts/check-branch-protection-drift.py`** — compares live settings with the desired file and emits `GOV-005` per difference; used by the weekly `governance-drift` schedule and runnable ad hoc.
- **Required-check name reconciliation** — a check that every name in `branch-protection.json` exists verbatim in the `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 table **and** (once E03 lands) as a job name in `.github/workflows/`; mismatch emits `GOV-005`. This closes the classic failure where a job is renamed and its "required" status silently evaporates.
- **Staged rollout plan, executed within this ticket**: phase 1 applies the review/linear-history/conversation/force-push settings plus only the checks that actually exist today (the `governance` job from E01-Q02); phase 2 (a checklist item completed during E03) adds each remaining §9 check as its job first goes green on `main`. The desired-state file carries a `pending:` annotation per not-yet-required check so the end state is visible and auditable from day 1.
- **Merge queue enabled** with the rebase-and-recheck flow described in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7.
- **Runbook** in the PR description and linked from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: how to break glass if protection must be bypassed in an emergency (who may, what must be recorded, and that the drift job will open an issue regardless).

## Out of scope

- Creating the CI jobs themselves — E03.
- Organisation-level rulesets or repository-creation policy.
- Protection for `release/*` branches — added at the first release cut (R1), tracked on E03/E07's release tooling.
- Any weakening of the constitution's review rules: if a setting proves unworkable, it goes through C-16.1 amendment, not a local exception (C-16.3).

**Security-control linkage (added per PR #1411 review, AC3):** this ticket is the owning delivery for SR-161 (branch protection MUST require CODEOWNERS review, verifiably distinguishable from a non-owner approval - `04-security-program.md` §6.17 / G1) and for G17's over-scoped-PAT mitigation (the administration credential is scoped to the minimum permission set, its use logged, and drift-checked). The acceptance criteria above (CODEOWNERS-insufficient scenario, admin-not-exempt scenario) already encode SR-161's behaviour; this note makes the SR <-> ticket traceability explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: An under-reviewed PR is unmergeable
  Given main protection has been applied from .github/branch-protection.json
  And a pull request has 1 approving review
  When the author attempts to merge or enqueue it
  Then GitHub refuses and states that 2 reviews are required

Scenario: A non-code-owner pair of approvals is insufficient
  Given a pull request touching a path owned by the chart-engine team
  And it has 2 approvals from engineers who are not code owners of that path
  When the author attempts to merge
  Then GitHub refuses, citing the required code-owner review

Scenario: Administrators are not exempt
  Given a repository administrator with a failing required check on their pull request
  When they attempt to merge
  Then the merge is refused, because enforce_admins is true

Scenario: Applying the configuration twice changes nothing
  Given the live settings already match .github/branch-protection.json
  When scripts/apply-branch-protection.py runs again
  Then it reports no changes and exits 0

Scenario: Drift is detected (failure path)
  Given someone disables "require review from Code Owners" in the GitHub UI
  When scripts/check-branch-protection-drift.py runs
  Then it prints GOV-005 naming the setting, the live value and the desired value
  And it exits non-zero so the scheduled job opens a priority/p1-high issue

Scenario: A renamed required check is caught
  Given branch-protection.json requires a check named unit-backend
  And no workflow defines a job with that name
  When the reconciliation check runs
  Then it reports GOV-005 for the missing job name
```

## Technical notes / design

Use the REST branch-protection endpoints (`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection`) plus the merge-queue settings; note that the full `PUT` is a **replace**, not a merge — so the desired-state file must be complete, and `--dry-run` must diff the whole object, not the delta the caller happens to care about. This is exactly why the configuration is a single committed file.

The credential needs repository administration scope; reuse the credential decided in ADR-0016 (E01-K01) if its scopes suffice, otherwise provision a separate, narrower one and record it. Never run the apply script automatically from a workflow triggered by a PR — it is invoked manually by an admin or by a `workflow_dispatch` with an environment approval, so a malicious PR cannot rewrite protection.

`pending:` annotation format inside the JSON (ignored by the API, read by the scripts):
```
"required_status_checks": {"strict": true, "contexts": ["governance"]},
"x-pending-contexts": ["lint", "typecheck", "unit-backend", "unit-engine", "unit-frontend", "contract", "integration", "e2e-smoke", "a11y", "sast", "sca", "secrets-scan", "container-scan", "license-check", "bundle-size", "engine-bench", "migrations", "architecture", "generated-code-check", "pr-metadata"]
```
The reconciliation check validates both lists against the §9 table, so the end state stays honest while the rollout is staged. Note the names are sourced *from* §9 (the single source of truth per C-16.5) — this file is a machine-readable projection, and the reconciliation check is what makes the projection safe rather than a duplicate.

## Test plan

- **Unit (pytest)**: diffing logic (added/removed/changed settings), `pending:` handling, reconciliation against a fixture §9 table and a fixture workflow directory, and refusal to apply an invalid desired file.
- **Integration**: apply → drift-check → mutate a setting via API → drift-check detects it → re-apply restores it, executed against a scratch repository.
- **E2E (manual, evidentiary)**: the four "unmergeable" scenarios executed once against the real repository with screenshots attached — this is the literal evidence for R0 exit criterion #1 and is collected by E01-Q01.
- **Chaos**: API failure mid-apply → assert the script reports the partial state clearly and is safe to re-run.
- Coverage target: ≥85% on `scripts/`.

## Security notes

Branch protection is the single control preventing unreviewed code from reaching `main`, and therefore every downstream security control (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13 supply chain). Threats and controls:
- **(T) Silent weakening** of protection by anyone with admin rights — mitigated by desired-state-as-code, weekly drift detection that opens a P1 issue, and an audit trail in git history.
- **(E) Privilege escalation via the apply credential** — the credential carries repository-administration scope and is the most powerful secret in E01; it is never exposed to PR-triggered workflows, is used only via manual/`workflow_dispatch`-with-approval, and its rotation owner is recorded. Reviewed in E01-X02.
- **(E) Admin bypass** — `enforce_admins: true` removes the exception entirely, consistent with C-9.1's "there is no 'admin merge'".
- **(D) Denial of delivery** — a required check that never reports blocks all merges; the staged rollout with `x-pending-contexts` is the mitigation, and the break-glass runbook covers the emergency case with mandatory recording.
Data classification: configuration metadata, no secrets in the file itself. Security-engineer review and sign-off required.

## Accessibility notes

N/A — no user interface. Script and drift-issue output is plain text with status written in words rather than colour.

## Performance notes

No runtime budget. Operationally, merge-queue rebase-and-recheck multiplies CI time by queue depth, so this Task records the expected queue throughput given the ≤15 min pipeline target from R0 exit criterion #2 and flags to E03 if the required-check set would make the queue the delivery bottleneck.

## Observability

- Weekly scheduled `governance-drift` workflow running the drift checker; any `GOV-005` opens a `priority/p1-high` issue tagged `security` and notifies the Owner.
- Every apply run archives a before/after diff as a CI artefact, giving a permanent record of protection changes independent of GitHub's own audit log.
- Break-glass usage is recorded as a comment on a dedicated tracking issue, reviewed at the R4 live-enablement gate.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified; the four "unmergeable" scenarios evidenced with screenshots (R0 exit criterion #1 evidence pack).
- [ ] `.github/branch-protection.json` applied; re-apply is a no-op; drift checker green.
- [ ] Required-check reconciliation green against `CONSTITUTION.md` §9; `x-pending-contexts` lists every not-yet-enabled check and E03 carries the checklist to graduate them.
- [ ] Merge queue enabled and demonstrated (one PR merged through it).
- [ ] Weekly drift schedule live and demonstrated firing on a deliberate mutation.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met for `scripts/`.
- [ ] Docs: break-glass runbook linked from `CONTRIBUTING.md`; no duplication of the §9 check list (checker green).
- [ ] Security: E01-X02 review of the admin credential complete; Security-engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] QA sign-off: E01-Q01 scenarios executed and recorded.
- [ ] Demo: an under-reviewed PR shown being refused at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T04` (code-owner review is meaningless until ownership is total — enabling it first would route sensitive reviews to the catch-all owner), `E01-T01` (rule references in the configuration and runbook must resolve), `E01-X01` (the STRIDE model covers the admin-credential and drift threats this Task must mitigate). Forward dependency on **E03** for the remaining required checks, handled via `x-pending-contexts` rather than by blocking.

## Branch

`feat/gov-branch-protection`. PR size: ~300 LOC of scripts/config plus tests; within guidance.

## Context

E01 introduces no product screens — `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 lists E01's `domains` and `modules` as `—`, and no `SCR-*` or `CMP-*` entry in `14-screens-catalogue.md`/`15-component-catalogue.md` belongs to it. But it does introduce a real, daily-use interface for ~15 engineers plus a large design org over 26 sprints: the **contributor surface** — the governance documents, the issue chooser, six issue forms, and the PR template. That surface decides whether the DoR/DoD data the entire board automation depends on is actually captured, or routed around.

This is a genuine design problem, not a formatting exercise. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` specifies 8–12 checklist items per Kind; naively transcribing them into forms produces a 40-field Story form that nobody completes honestly, which yields garbage data and guards that block on technicalities. The design job is to decide **what is captured at creation vs at Ready vs at Done**, what is a required field vs a prompt, and how the gate-relevant sections are labelled so they are both human-obvious and machine-parsable (the contract E01-T05 implements and E01-T07 parses).

**Design-ahead note (the full, signed waiver record is the dedicated section below):** the standard rule (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1) requires design Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming engineering ticket. E01 lands in Sprint 01 — there is no Sprint −1. This is the documented exception case: an explicit Architect/CDO waiver is recorded on this ticket per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1, justified because (a) the surface is contributor-facing, not customer-facing, (b) it has no dependency on design-system v0 (E05), and (c) delaying it would delay every other epic's ticket hygiene. Design and implementation run in the same sprint with design landing first in the sprint, and the design-QA follow-up (E01-D02) lands in Sprint 02.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **UX research (lightweight, `ux-research` label)** — 4–6 × 20-minute interviews across the disciplines that will file tickets (backend, frontend, chart-engine, QA, DevSecOps, security, design). Questions: what killed ticket hygiene at your last project; which fields you would fake to get past a form; what you need to see in a ticket to start work without asking. Output: a findings note with the top 5 friction points, in `docs/plan/backlog/schema/README.md`'s design-rationale section or a linked Figma/FigJam board.
- **Information architecture** for the contributor surface: which document answers which question, and the single entry point (`CONTRIBUTING.md`) with a one-hop path to everything else. Delivered as an IA diagram plus a one-page "where do I look for X" table that E01-T02 implements.
- **Field-set specification per Kind** (Epic, Story, Task, Spike, Bug, Chore): every field with its label text, help text, required/optional, control type (dropdown/textarea/input/checkboxes), default, and the DoR item from `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` it satisfies — or an explicit note that the item is verified at Ready/Done rather than captured at creation. **Hard constraint: the Task form is completable in under 2 minutes.**
- **Gate-section contract** — the exact heading text for `### QA sign-off`, `### Security review`, `### a11y evidence`, `### Acceptance criteria`, `### Test plan`, agreed jointly with the E01-T07 owner so parsing is deterministic.
- **PR template wireframe** — section order, the checklist ceiling (~60 lines), and which items link out versus state inline.
- **Writing-style spec** for help text: imperative, specific, gives the constraint in words, no jargon without a link, no colour/emoji-only meaning.
- **Motion:** N/A — GitHub-rendered surfaces expose no motion control.
- **Sign-off criteria** listed under Definition of Done below.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the forms/templates — E01-T05 (this is the `handoff` artefact it consumes).
- Design-system tokens, components, Figma libraries — E05; this surface is rendered by GitHub and cannot use them.
- Any product screen, flow or component.
- The board's own column/field layout in GitHub Projects (repo admin configuration, informed by E01-K01).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every DoR item is accounted for
  Given the per-Kind DoR checklists in docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md
  When the field-set specification is reviewed
  Then each checklist item maps to a form field, or to an explicit "verified at Ready/Done, not captured at creation" note
  And no item is silently dropped

Scenario: The Task form respects the time budget
  Given the specified Task form field set
  When three engineers file a representative Task against the paper prototype
  Then each completes it in under 2 minutes
  And none reports a field they would fabricate to get past validation

Scenario: Gate sections are agreed with the automation owner
  Given the gate-section heading contract
  When the E01-T07 owner reviews it
  Then every heading is confirmed parsable and stable
  And the absent-versus-empty distinction is explicitly specified

Scenario: Research findings changed the design (evidence of a real research pass)
  Given the interview findings note
  When the field-set specification is reviewed against it
  Then at least one specific design decision cites a specific finding
  And rejected findings are recorded with the reason for rejection
```

## Design-ahead waiver (Architect/CDO) — explicit record

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires a linked design artefact to have been **Done for ≥2 sprints** before the consuming ticket starts, *or* an explicit Architect/CDO waiver recorded with a reason. This chain — `E01-D01` (design, Sprint 01) → `E01-T05` (build, Sprint 01) → `E01-D02` (design-QA, Sprint 02) — runs at a 0–1 sprint gap, so the waiver path applies and is recorded here explicitly rather than left implicit in the Kind=Task classification.

- **Waiver granted by:** Architect (repo/architecture owner) and CDO, at Sprint 01 planning; both countersign as a ticket comment before this ticket leaves Ready.
- **Scope of waiver:** the E01 contributor surface only — `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and the rendered governance markdown. It does **not** extend to any `SCR-*` product screen; every customer-facing screen from E05 onward observes the full 2-sprint rule with no exception.
- **Reasons (all four hold):**
  1. **No Sprint −1 exists.** E01 is the first ticket set of the first sprint of the programme; a 2-sprint lead time is arithmetically unavailable and no sequencing creates it.
  2. **Contributor-facing, not customer-facing.** The audience is the delivery team plus reviewers. Iteration cost is one PR against a YAML file, the feedback loop is hours rather than a release train, and there is no migration, no stored user state and no public commitment to the layout.
  3. **No design-system dependency.** These surfaces are rendered by GitHub's own chrome — the design freedom is information architecture, field set, wording and required flags, none of which consume the design-system v0 tokens delivered in E05.   - Design lands **first within Sprint 01** — `E01-D01` must be Status=Done before `E01-T05` opens a PR; `blocked_by` enforces the ordering even though the sprint is shared.

- **Coverage review**: the DoR-item → field mapping table is walked line by line with the Architect and QA lead.
- **Parsability review**: the gate-section contract walked with the E01-T07 owner.
- **a11y review** of the specified labels/help text against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (full audit of the built artefact happens in E01-D02).
- No automated tests (design artefact); the built implementation is tested in E01-T05.

## Security notes

The design determines whether contributors are *invited* to paste sensitive data into a public-ish surface. Required by design: every form carries an explicit "never paste API keys, session cookies, tokens, or real account identifiers" warning in its description; the Bug form's repro-steps help text explicitly says to redact account ids and keys; the issue chooser routes vulnerability reports to the private channel in `SECURITY.md` and no form invites vulnerability details. The design must also avoid presenting sign-offs (QA/security) as author-fillable fields, because that would make forgery the path of least resistance — recorded here as a design decision with its rationale, implemented in E01-T05/T07. Data classification: public-internal metadata. Reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E01-X01's surface review.

## Accessibility notes

This is an owned surface under `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (which is explicit that there is no "internal tool" exemption — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). Design requirements specified here and audited in E01-D02: every field has a real, persistent label (never placeholder-as-label); help text conveys constraints in words, not colour or emoji; required state is programmatic (`validations: required`), not a visual asterisk; dropdown option text is self-describing out of context; heading hierarchy in the rendered body is correctly nested and starts at `###` under the issue title; link text is descriptive; no meaning carried by emoji or colour alone; tables have header rows.

## Performance notes

The budget is human time, and it is a real budget: **Task form ≤2 minutes, Story form ≤5 minutes, PR template ≤3 minutes** to complete honestly. Measured in the usability test. A form that exceeds its budget is redesigned, not shipped with a plea for discipline — over-long forms are the mechanism by which ticket data becomes fiction.

## Observability

Specify which signals tell us the design failed in production, so E01-Q02 can watch them: rate of issues created outside the forms (target zero once blank issues are disabled), rate of guard blocks caused by a missing section rather than genuine non-compliance (a false-positive proxy — target zero over the observe-only period), and median time-to-Ready (a rising trend suggests the forms capture too little).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Research findings note published with top-5 friction points and the interview participants' disciplines.
- [ ] IA diagram + "where do I look for X" table delivered.
- [ ] Per-Kind field-set specification complete, with every DoR item mapped or explicitly deferred.
- [ ] Gate-section heading contract agreed and signed by the E01-T07 owner.
- [ ] PR template wireframe delivered with the checklist ceiling respected.
- [ ] Usability test executed; time budgets met; findings incorporated or rejected-with-reason.
- [ ] a11y requirements specified per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- [ ] **Design sign-off: CDO approves at Design Review** (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3 weekly Wed Design Review) — this is the gate for Status=Done.
- [ ] Architect/CDO **design-ahead waiver recorded on the ticket** with its reason (no Sprint −1 exists; see Context).
- [ ] Handoff delivered to E01-T05's owner: annotated spec, field table, states (empty/required-error/submitted), and the gate-section contract.
- [ ] Security engineer has reviewed the "do not paste secrets" warnings and the report-diversion design.

## Dependencies

No blockers — runs first in Sprint 01. Blocks `E01-T05` (implementation) and, transitively, `E01-T07` (which parses what T05 renders). Relies on the DoR/DoD content of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` and the label taxonomy of `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2 being locked, which they are.

## Branch

`design/gov-contributor-ia` (design artefacts committed as markdown + linked FigJam). PR size: small; spec documents only.

## References

- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1 design-ahead rule, §3 Design Review, §5.1 Kinds, §5.2 labels
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §§2–7 per-Kind DoR, §3.1 design-ready waiver path, §8 gating notes
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (tone/writing conventions; tokens N/A on this surface)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (E01 has no domains/modules — no product screens)
- `SECURITY.md`

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1 design-ahead rule, §3 Design Review, §5.1 Kinds, §5.2 labels

4. `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (tone/writing conventions; tokens N/A on this surface)
5. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (E01 has no domains/modules — no product screens)
6. `SECURITY.md`

- `docs/plan/`
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/research/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint (markdown lint job)`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/gov-contributor-ia`
- PR title: "E01-D01: Design the contributor information architecture and issue-form field set"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: type/task, area/docs, priority/p1-high, design, ux-research, handoff, a11y

**Done means**
- Research findings note published with top-5 friction points and the interview participants' disciplines.
- IA diagram + "where do I look for X" table delivered.
- Per-Kind field-set specification complete, with every DoR item mapped or explicitly deferred.
- Gate-section heading contract agreed and signed by the E01-T07 owner.
- PR template wireframe delivered with the checklist ceiling respected.
- Usability test executed; time budgets met; findings incorporated or rejected-with-reason.

**Do NOT**
- Implementing the forms/templates — E01-T05 (this is the `handoff` artefact it consumes).
- Design-system tokens, components, Figma libraries — E05; this surface is rendered by GitHub and cannot use them.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

E01's UI surface is the contributor surface specified in **E01-D01** and built in **E01-T05** (issue forms, issue chooser, PR template) and **E01-T07** (automation comments, which are the automation's entire user interface). This ticket is the verification pass: does what shipped match what was designed, and is it accessible to a screen-reader or keyboard-only contributor? A contributor who cannot file a ticket cannot participate in this project at all — this is an inclusion gate, not a polish pass.

It runs in Sprint 02, one sprint after the build, which is the normal design-QA cadence. - **Rendered-output review** of the E01-T07 automation comments: plain-text readable, status stated in words (not colour/emoji alone), heading/list structure correct, actionable next step present.
- **Governance-document markdown pass**: `CONSTITUTION.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — single H1, correctly nested headings, header-row tables, descriptive link text, and a prose summary adjacent to every mermaid diagram (rendered diagrams are images without accessible text).

- Reconciliation: if the build diverged from the spec for a good reason, the E01-D01 spec is updated so the record reflects what shipped (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 docs rule).

## Out of scope

- Fixing GitHub's own product accessibility — out of our control; such findings are recorded as "platform limitation, accepted" with the reason, and only our *content* choices are treated as defects.
- Product screens/components — none exist in E01; the R0 product a11y gate (Storybook + auth/shell routes) belongs to E05/E09/E10.
- axe-core CI wiring — E03 ships the `a11y` job for the web app; GitHub-hosted surfaces cannot be axe-scanned by us, so this pass is manual by necessity, and that constraint is stated in the findings report rather than left as an implied gap.

```gherkin
  Given the shipped issue forms and the E01-D01 field-set specification
  When a design-system-trained reviewer compares them field by field
  Then every discrepancy is either fixed or filed as a Bug with a priority label
  And the comparison table is attached to this ticket

Scenario: Every form is completable keyboard-only
  Given a contributor using only the keyboard
  When they navigate from the issue chooser through each of the six forms and submit
  Then every control is reachable and operable with a visible focus indicator
  And no step requires a pointer

Scenario: Required state is announced, not merely shown (failure path)
  Given a screen-reader user submits the Story form with acceptance criteria empty
  When the validation error appears
  Then the error is announced and associated with the offending field
  And if it is not, a finding is raised at P2 minimum with the responsible content fix or an accepted platform-limitation note

Scenario: Automation comments carry no colour-only meaning
  Given a blocked-close comment produced by the E01-T07 guards
  When it is read as plain text with images and emoji suppressed
  Then the decision and the required next step are fully understandable

Scenario: Every governance diagram has a text equivalent
  Given all mermaid diagrams in the governance documents
  When each is reviewed
  Then each has adjacent prose conveying the same information
  And any that does not is fixed in this ticket
```

  2. **Contributor-facing, not customer-facing.** The audience is the delivery team plus reviewers. Iteration cost is one PR against a YAML file, the feedback loop is hours rather than a release train, and there is no migration, no stored user state and no public commitment to the layout.

  - Any discrepancy found in D02 is fixed or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*`, so the shortened lead time surfaces as tracked defects rather than silent quality loss.
- **Expiry:** this waiver covers E01 only and sets no precedent. If a second Sprint-01-style exception is requested in R0, the Architect raises it at the R0 retro as a proposed standing amendment to `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1 instead of granting waivers case-by-case.

## Technical notes / design

Method: scripted walkthrough with a recorded session (screen capture + NVDA audio) so findings are reviewable asynchronously by the CDO and the a11y specialist rather than re-performed. Use the `03-testing-strategy.md` §12 protocol and the acceptance-criteria template in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §10 for phrasing findings.

Where GitHub's rendering limits us (e.g. no control over focus styling in their UI), classify precisely: **content defect** (ours, fix it) versus **platform limitation** (theirs, record and accept). Blurring the two is how a11y debt becomes invisible, so each finding must be explicitly one or the other.

For the markdown pass, a mechanical pre-check (heading-level sequence, table header rows, bare-URL link text, mermaid blocks without adjacent prose) can be scripted quickly and folded into the `governance` job by E01-Q02 if it proves useful — propose it as a follow-up rather than expanding this ticket.

## Test plan

- **Manual a11y**: keyboard-only pass (all six forms + chooser + PR template); NVDA pass (Story form + chooser); plain-text/no-emoji reading of automation comments.
- **Design-QA**: field-by-field comparison table against the D01 spec.
- **Mechanical**: heading/link/table/diagram checks over the five governance documents.
- **Regression**: findings that are fixable in content are re-verified after the fix; a follow-up check is added to E01-Q02 where automatable.
- No unit tests (verification ticket, not code). Coverage: N/A.

## Security notes

Verify, as part of the same pass, two security-relevant content behaviours designed in E01-D01: (a) every form displays the "never paste API keys, tokens, session cookies or real account identifiers" warning, and it is announced by a screen reader rather than being a visual-only aside; (b) the issue chooser diverts vulnerability reports to the private route in `SECURITY.md` and no form invites vulnerability details. A missing or invisible warning is a **security finding**, not a cosmetic one, and is raised at P2 minimum. Data classification: public-internal metadata.

## Accessibility notes

This ticket *is* the accessibility review. Conformance target **WCAG 2.2 AA** per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1. Specific criteria exercised: 1.3.1 info & relationships (label/field association, heading structure, table headers), 1.4.1 use of colour (status in words), 2.1.1 keyboard, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.4 link purpose, 2.4.7 focus visible, 3.3.1/3.3.2 error identification and labels/instructions, 4.1.3 status messages (guard comments and validation errors). Findings use the `05-accessibility-standard.md` §10 acceptance-criteria template and the §11.3 severity taxonomy with P2 as the floor for any AA violation.

## Performance notes

N/A — no runtime surface. The human-time budgets from E01-D01 (Task ≤2 min, Story ≤5 min, PR ≤3 min) are re-measured on the *built* forms during the keyboard pass, since keyboard-only completion time is the honest worst case and would reveal a form that is only fast with a mouse.

## Observability

Findings are recorded as issues with the `a11y` label, which means E01-T07's a11y guard applies to their own closure — they cannot be closed without evidence, which is a pleasing and deliberate self-application of the epic's own control. The findings report is archived under the epic for the R0 quality-gate evidence pack (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 A11y row).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Design-QA comparison table attached; all discrepancies fixed or filed with priorities.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and NVDA passes executed; session recordings attached.
- [ ] Automation-comment and governance-document passes complete; content fixes merged.
- [ ] Findings report published with severities and a clear content-defect vs platform-limitation classification.
- [ ] Any WCAG 2.2 AA violation is fixed or has a recorded, justified acceptance (P2 minimum severity, never silently closed).
- [ ] E01-D01 spec updated where the build legitimately diverged.
- [ ] Waiver compensating controls audited: confirm D01 was Done before T05’s PR, the mid-sprint walkthrough happened, and every delta reached the spec — any gap recorded as a retro input for the R0 review of the design-ahead rule.
- [ ] **Design sign-off: CDO accepts at Design Review; a11y specialist signs off on the accessibility findings.**
- [ ] Security: the no-secrets warning and report-diversion checks verified; findings routed to the Security engineer if failing.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (this ticket's own verification is the evidence; QA reviews the report).
- [ ] PR(s) with content fixes merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T05` (the built forms and PR template), `E01-T07` (the automation comments that form the guards' user interface), `E01-D01` (the specification being verified against). title: Author and execute the governance conformance test plan and exploratory charter
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 requires a black-box test plan per story group, authored or reviewed by QA **before** development completes, and §11.2 requires a time-boxed exploratory charter per epic. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 exit criterion #1 demands demonstrated evidence that an under-reviewed PR is unmergeable and that no path is un-owned — evidence somebody must actually produce, from the outside, without reading the implementation.

That is this ticket. Governance controls have a specific and dangerous failure mode: they *appear* to work because nothing visibly breaks. A guard that silently passes, a required check that is required-in-name-only after a job rename, a CODEOWNERS rule that matches nothing — all look identical to "working" from the inside. Black-box verification by someone who did not write the scripts is the only way to distinguish them.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Black-box test plan** (committed at `docs/plan/backlog/testplans/E01-governance.md`) covering every governance control shipped by E01, written from the outside — actions and observable outcomes only, no reference to script internals:
  - **Branch protection (E01-T08)**: merge with 1 approval; merge with 2 non-code-owner approvals; merge as an administrator with a red check; force-push to `main`; delete `main`; merge with an unresolved conversation; merge a non-linear-history PR; merge-queue rebase-and-recheck behaviour.
  - **Ownership (E01-T04)**: add an un-owned path → checker fails; confirm GitHub's own "Owners" resolution agrees with the checker for three sample paths.
  - **Rule references & duplication (E01-T01)**: introduce a dangling `C-99.9`; duplicate five required-check names into `CONTRIBUTING.md`; confirm both fail and that the messages are actionable by someone who has never seen the script.
  - **Ticket schema (E01-T06)**: submit a ticket missing `perspective`; a `blocked_by` pointing nowhere; a dependency cycle; an `estimate` of 13 on a Story; a design ticket scheduled one sprint (not two) ahead of its consumer.
  - **Board guards (E01-T07)**: close a Story with no QA sign-off; close with a sign-off comment from a non-QA member; close with the marker typed in the body by the author (forgery); close a `security` ticket without a security-team comment; open an `area/auth-rbac` issue without the `security` label and confirm auto-labelling; close an `a11y` ticket with a foreign link; force an API error and confirm fail-closed.
  - **Templates (E01-T05)**: submit each form with required fields empty; confirm blank issues are disabled; confirm the vulnerability-report diversion link.
  Each case: preconditions, steps, expected observable result, actual, pass/fail, evidence link.
- **Exploratory charter** (60–120 min, `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 format — mission, areas to probe, oracles, debrief): *"Probe the governance controls for bypasses: can a determined, non-malicious engineer in a hurry get non-compliant work onto main or close a ticket without its gates?"* Oracles: a merge that should not have happened; a closed ticket missing its evidence; a guard that stayed silent; a confusing error that would drive someone to route around the process.
- **Cold-read usability verification** of `CONTRIBUTING.md` (feeding E01-T02's acceptance criteria): one engineer who has not read the constitution goes clone → branch → commit → PR using only that document; every confusion point recorded.
- **Evidence pack** for R0 exit criterion #1: screenshots/recordings of each refused merge, archived under the epic.
- **Bug tickets** for every failure found, with severity per §11.3.
- **QA sign-off comment** on E01 and on each child, per `03-testing-strategy.md` §16.

## Out of scope

- Automating these checks in CI — **E01-Q02** (this ticket establishes what to automate by executing it manually first, which is the right order: automating an unvalidated check just encodes the bug).
- Testing E03's pipeline jobs — E03's own QA.
- Security abuse cases requiring adversarial privilege (token theft, malicious workflow injection) — **E01-X01/X02**; this charter covers the "engineer in a hurry", not the attacker.
- Product/feature testing — none exists yet.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The test plan exists before the controls are declared done
  Given the governance controls shipped by E01
  When any child ticket reaches In Test
  Then the black-box test plan already contains its cases
  And the plan was authored or reviewed by QA rather than by the implementer alone

Scenario: Every documented control is proven from the outside
  Given the full test plan
  When QA executes it against the real repository
  Then every case has a recorded actual result and a pass or fail verdict
  And every pass has an evidence link (screenshot, run URL, or command transcript)

Scenario: An under-reviewed merge is demonstrably refused
  Given a pull request with a single approval
  When QA attempts to merge it
  Then the merge is refused and a screenshot is captured
  And that screenshot forms part of the R0 exit-criterion-1 evidence pack

Scenario: A bypass found during exploration is filed, not absorbed (failure path)
  Given the exploratory session discovers a way to close a Story without QA sign-off
  When the session debrief is written
  Then a Bug is filed with severity per docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md section 11.3
  And the epic cannot reach Done while that Bug is open at P0 or P1

Scenario: Error messages are actionable to a newcomer
  Given each governance checker failure message
  When a contributor who has never seen the scripts reads it
  Then they can state what to change without asking the implementer
  And any message failing this is filed as a P2 usability bug
```

## Technical notes / design

Execution environment: a **scratch repository** mirroring the real repo's protection and workflows for the destructive cases (force-push, branch deletion, administrator-merge attempts) — those must never be attempted against the real `main`. The non-destructive cases (refused merges, guard behaviour on throwaway issues) run against the real repository, because testing the copy proves only that the copy works; the R0 evidence pack requires the real one. Which cases run where is stated explicitly per case in the plan.

The forged-sign-off and fail-closed cases are the highest-value in the plan: they are the two failure modes that would leave the whole gating structure decorative. Fail-closed is provoked by revoking the guard's credential temporarily on the scratch repo, not by waiting for an outage.

Test plan lives in the repository (not a wiki) so it versions with the controls, consistent with `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1's principle that plans travel with the ticket; the plan file is linked from each child ticket's Test plan section.

## Test plan

This ticket *is* a test plan; verification is that it was executed and evidenced. Meta-checks: every E01 child ticket's acceptance criteria appear as at least one case here (traceability table at the top of the plan, mapping ticket key → case ids); any case that cannot be executed is marked blocked with the reason rather than quietly dropped.

## Security notes

QA must not create real credentials, real Bybit keys, or real secrets while testing — all fixtures are obviously-fake strings. The credential-revocation test for fail-closed behaviour is performed on the **scratch** repository only, and the revoked credential is confirmed re-issued/restored afterwards with a recorded check, since a half-restored guard credential is a silent governance outage. Findings with a security character (a genuine bypass of the security-close guard, an over-permissive token observed in a log) are routed immediately to the Security engineer and tracked under E01-X01/X02 rather than as ordinary bugs. Data classification: public-internal metadata only.

## Accessibility notes

The keyboard-only and screen-reader verification of the contributor surfaces is owned by **E01-D02**, not duplicated here. This ticket contributes one adjacent check: that every governance failure message is comprehensible as plain text without colour or emoji, which is both an a11y and a usability property.

## Performance notes

Record, as observed data rather than as a target: the wall-clock time for each guard to react (feeding E01-T07's 30 s decision budget) and the total governance-job duration (feeding the epic's ≤60 s budget). Slow gates are a real risk to the ≤15 min pipeline in R0 exit criterion #2, and QA's measurements are the evidence.

## Observability

The executed plan and the charter debrief are the epic's QA evidence, archived under E01 for the R0 quality-gate pack (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4). Every bug filed references the failing case id, so the regression pack in E01-Q02 can be traced back to a real observed failure rather than a speculative one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Test plan committed at `docs/plan/backlog/testplans/E01-governance.md` with a ticket→case traceability table.
- [ ] All cases executed with recorded actual results and evidence links; blocked cases justified.
- [ ] Exploratory charter executed (60–120 min) and debrief note attached to the epic.
- [ ] Cold-read usability verification of `CONTRIBUTING.md` executed; findings fed to E01-T02.
- [ ] R0 exit-criterion-1 evidence pack assembled.
- [ ] Bugs filed for every failure with correct severity; no open P0/P1 against E01 scope.
- [ ] Automatable cases handed to **E01-Q02** as a prioritised list.
- [ ] QA sign-off comments posted on E01 and each child ticket, per `03-testing-strategy.md` §16.
- [ ] Findings presented at the Sprint 01 review.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T08` (branch protection must be applied before it can be black-box tested — it is the centrepiece of the evidence pack) and `E01-T01` (the checkers must exist to be probed). Cases covering E01-T04/T05/T06/T07 are executed as those tickets land, in the order they land; the plan is authored up front so no control reaches In Test without its cases already written. Blocks `E01-Q02` (which automates the validated cases).

## Branch

`chore/gov-test-plan` for the plan document; test execution produces no production code. PR size: small.

title: Ship the governance regression pack as a required CI job
body:
## Context

E01 ships five independent checkers (`check-rule-refs`, `check-sot-duplication`, `check-codeowners-coverage`, `validate-backlog`, plus the issue-form schema/parser tests) and four board guards. E01-Q01 proves they work **once**, by hand. Without automation they decay: a new directory lands un-owned, an enum drifts from `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2, a form field is renamed and a guard silently stops finding its section.

`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #20 assigns the rule-reference and single-source-list checks to the `pr-metadata` required check; §9 also requires that required-check names be exact and stable. This ticket assembles E01's checks into one coherent, fast, required job and connects it to E01-T08's protection configuration, closing the loop between "we wrote a rule", "we wrote a checker", and "the checker actually blocks a merge".

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`.github/workflows/governance.yml`** defining a job named exactly **`governance`** (the name is added to `.github/branch-protection.json` by E01-T08, and the reconciliation check in T08 verifies the two agree) that runs on every PR and on `main`, executing:
  1. `scripts/check-rule-refs.sh` (`GOV-002`)
  2. `scripts/check-sot-duplication.py` (`GOV-003`)
  3. `scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py` (`GOV-001`)
  4. `scripts/validate-backlog.py` (`GOV-004`)
  5. issue-form schema validation + rendered-body parser contract tests (E01-T05/T07 shared fixtures)
  6. `scripts/check-branch-protection-drift.py --offline` (config-vs-§9 reconciliation only; the live-API drift comparison stays on the weekly schedule, since PR jobs must not require an admin credential — `GOV-005`)
  7. markdownlint over governance documents + relative-link resolution
- **Unit-test suite for all `scripts/`** wired into the same job with the ≥85% coverage gate (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #3 threshold applied to Python).
- **Regression cases from E01-Q01** — every manually-validated case that can be automated is encoded as a test with a comment naming its originating case id, so each automated check traces to a real observed failure.
- **Canary self-tests** — the job proves it can still fail: a `--self-test` mode runs each checker against a deliberately-broken fixture tree and asserts a non-zero exit. This is the guard against the worst outcome, a green check that no longer checks anything.
- **`.github/workflows/governance-drift.yml`** — weekly schedule running the live branch-protection drift check and a workflow-enabled check; opens a `priority/p1-high` `security`-labelled issue on drift.
- **Artefacts** — ownership report (E01-T04 `--report`) and backlog summary (E01-T06 `--summary`) uploaded per run for diffable history.
- **Runbook section** in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (one paragraph + link): what each `GOV-00n` code means and how to fix it locally.

## Out of scope

- The other 19 required checks in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 — E03.
- Enabling `governance` as *required* in branch protection — that edit belongs to E01-T08's configuration file; this ticket delivers the job and confirms the name matches.
- Load/perf testing of the product (k6/Locust) — `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` scope, not governance.
- Board-guard integration tests against the live repository — those live with E01-T07; only its pure parser/evaluator units run here.

**Security-control linkage (added per PR #1411 review, AC3):** this ticket is the owning delivery for SR-163 (issue/PR bodies MUST be in the secret-scanning surface, via `validate-backlog`'s secret-pattern scan - `04-security-program.md` §6.17 / G11), for G14's credential-expiry mitigation (the weekly drift job proactively checks the E01-T07 guard credential's validity and alerts before it lapses), and for G17's drift-detection half (alerting if the E01-T08 credential's actual scopes exceed its documented scope). Add explicit test-plan coverage for a credential-expiry-alert case (G14) and a scope-drift-alert case (G17) alongside the existing drift scenarios in the Acceptance criteria above.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The governance job blocks a non-compliant pull request
  Given a pull request that adds a directory with no CODEOWNERS rule
  When the governance job runs
  Then it fails with GOV-001 naming the offending path
  And the pull request cannot be merged once the job is required

Scenario: The job proves it can still fail
  Given the --self-test mode with deliberately broken fixtures
  When the governance job runs it
  Then every checker returns a non-zero exit against its broken fixture
  And the job fails if any checker reports success against a known-bad fixture

Scenario: The job is fast enough not to be the bottleneck
  Given a normal pull request
  When the governance job runs on CI
  Then it completes in 60 seconds or less
  And the measured duration is recorded as a job annotation

Scenario: The required-check name matches the protection configuration
  Given .github/branch-protection.json and .github/workflows/governance.yml
  When the offline reconciliation check runs
  Then the job name governance appears identically in both
  And a rename in either file alone fails the check with GOV-005

Scenario: Backlog drift across epics is caught (failure path)
  Given another epic's backlog file introduces a blocked_by pointing at a key that does not exist
  When the governance job runs on that pull request
  Then validate-backlog fails with GOV-004 naming the unresolvable dependency
  And the pull request is blocked until it is fixed

Scenario: Weekly drift detection opens an issue
  Given someone disables require-code-owner-review in the GitHub UI
  When the weekly governance-drift workflow runs
  Then it opens a priority/p1-high security-labelled issue naming the changed setting
```

## Technical notes / design

Single job, not seven — one required check whose log is read top to bottom, with each checker emitting a clear section header and its `GOV-00n` codes. Seven separate required checks would multiply merge-queue overhead for no diagnostic gain.

Run order is cheapest-first with **no fail-fast**: all checkers run even if an earlier one fails, so a contributor sees every problem in one iteration instead of a drip-feed of CI failures. The job fails if any checker failed.

Exit-code discipline from E01-T01 is load-bearing here: exit 2 (internal error) must fail the job, never be treated as clean. The self-test mode exists specifically because a crashing checker that exits 0 is indistinguishable from a passing one in a green tick.

Python setup avoids a full E02 toolchain dependency (E02 lands in parallel): the job uses `actions/setup-python` with a pinned version and installs only `jsonschema` from a pinned, hash-checked requirements file, so governance CI works before the monorepo tooling exists and does not break when it arrives. All actions pinned to full commit SHAs (`04-security-program.md` §6.13).

`permissions:` is `contents: read` only for the PR job; the drift job additionally needs `issues: write`. Neither needs an admin credential, which is why the live-API drift comparison is split onto the scheduled workflow with its own environment-protected secret.

## Test plan

- **Unit**: all `scripts/` tests, ≥85% line coverage, run inside this job.
- **Contract**: issue-form schema validation and the rendered-body parser fixtures shared with E01-T05/T07 — the check that catches a form change silently breaking a guard.
- **Regression**: automated encodings of E01-Q01's validated cases, each annotated with its originating case id.
- **Meta/canary**: `--self-test` against broken fixtures, asserting each checker fails; a mutation check that removing a checker invocation from the workflow is caught (the workflow lists its checkers in a manifest the self-test compares against).
- **Perf**: job duration asserted ≤60 s, recorded per run.
- **Chaos**: simulate a checker crashing (exit 2) and assert the job fails rather than passing.

## Security notes

A CI job is executable code running on every PR and is therefore a supply-chain surface (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13, §6.14). Controls: least-privilege `permissions:` per job; all actions SHA-pinned; pinned hash-checked Python dependencies; no secrets in the PR-triggered job (so a fork or untrusted branch cannot exfiltrate one); no `pull_request_target`; checkers treat all repository content as data and never execute it. The drift workflow's admin credential lives behind a protected environment and is reviewed in E01-X02. Additional security value delivered: `validate-backlog`'s secret-pattern scan over ticket bodies and the `governance-drift` alert are both detective controls for the R4 live-enablement evidence. Security-engineer review required on the workflow files.

## Accessibility notes

CI output is a read surface for every contributor: failures are written as words with `GOV-00n` codes and an explicit fix instruction, never colour- or emoji-only; GitHub annotations carry file and line so the failure is navigable rather than requiring visual log scanning. Consistent with `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.

## Performance notes

**Budget: the `governance` job completes in ≤60 s** (the epic-level budget), protecting R0 exit criterion #2's ≤15 min commit-to-dev pipeline. Per-checker budgets inherited from their tickets: rule-refs and duplication ≤5 s, CODEOWNERS coverage ≤5 s, backlog validation ≤10 s. Duration is recorded per run as an annotation so regression is visible; exceeding the budget is treated as a defect against this ticket, not as an accepted cost — because a slow required check is the thing that makes a merge queue unusable.

## Observability

- Per-run artefacts: ownership report, backlog summary, coverage report, job duration.
- Stable `GOV-00n` codes across all checkers make CI history greppable for trend analysis.
- Weekly drift job as the detective control for protection/workflow tampering, escalating to a P1 issue.
- Metrics worth watching from R0 (noted for the retro): governance-job failure rate by code, median job duration, and the count of `# future:`-marked CODEOWNERS rules still outstanding.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `governance` job live, running on every PR, name matching `.github/branch-protection.json` (reconciliation green).
- [ ] All checkers, unit tests and the coverage gate (≥85% on `scripts/`) run inside it.
- [ ] Self-test/canary mode implemented and demonstrated failing against broken fixtures.
- [ ] Every automatable case from E01-Q01 encoded, each annotated with its originating case id; non-automatable cases listed with reasons.
- [ ] Weekly `governance-drift` workflow live and demonstrated opening an issue on a deliberate mutation.
- [ ] perf: job duration measured and ≤60 s, recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `GOV-00n` runbook paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `AGENTS.md` §4 command entries current; no duplicated owned lists.
- [ ] Security: workflows reviewed by the Security engineer (E01-X02), actions SHA-pinned, permissions least-privilege.
- [ ] QA sign-off: QA confirms the automated pack reproduces the manual results from E01-Q01.
- [ ] Demo: a non-compliant PR shown being blocked by the `governance` check at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-Q01` (automate only what has been manually validated — encoding an unvalidated check just enshrines the bug), `E01-T06` (the backlog validator is a component of the job), `E01-T07` (the parser/evaluator units and shared form fixtures). Coordinates with `E01-T08`, which owns adding `governance` to the required-check list, and with **E03**, which owns the remaining 19 checks; this job must not duplicate E03's work, only E01's controls.

## Branch

`feat/gov-regression-pack`. PR size: workflow + test wiring ≈ 300 LOC; within guidance.

## References

- `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 (required checks, #3 coverage, #20 `pr-metadata`), C-9.3 flaky-test policy, C-16.4, C-16.5
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §2 pyramid targets, §11 black-box QA, §14 flaky-test policy, §15 coverage gates
