title: STRIDE threat model for the repository, CI and board administration surface
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires a STRIDE threat-model kickoff for any epic labelled `security`, and `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes "threat model STRIDE per epic" a non-negotiable SDLC requirement. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 already models ten product areas (API keys, order path, rule engine, fan-out, WS, auth/RBAC, admin screens, recorder, Electron, network) — but **not the development and governance surface itself**, and §6.13/§6.14 cover supply chain and CI secrets as requirements without a threat model behind them.

That gap matters more here than in most projects. CandleViewer handles exchange API keys and live order flow; the repository and its CI are the upstream of every one of those controls. An attacker (or a careless insider) who can merge unreviewed code, alter a workflow, or weaken branch protection defeats every downstream control in `04-security-program.md` without touching a single runtime asset. E01 is also the epic that *creates* privileged automation (E01-T07's guard credential, E01-T08's repository-administration credential), so it must be modelled before those are built — hence this ticket blocks both.

## Scope / Deliverables

A STRIDE model committed as a new section of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (**§5.12 — Area 11: Development, CI and governance surface**, keeping that document the single owner of the STRIDE content per C-16.5), covering:

- **Assets**: repository contents; `main` branch integrity; branch-protection configuration; CODEOWNERS; workflow definitions; the E01-T07 guard credential; the E01-T08 administration credential; Actions secrets in general; the GitHub Project board and its data; the backlog JSON tree; release tags and artefacts (forward-looking to E03).
- **Actors and trust levels**: Owner (`@basiltt`), engineers, contractors, **AI coding agents acting under `AGENTS.md`**, GitHub as a platform, third-party Actions authors, dependency maintainers.
- **Trust boundaries**: developer workstation → GitHub; PR from a branch vs from a fork; workflow runner → repository write scope; GitHub Projects API → board data; committed governance config → live platform settings (the drift boundary). Extends the TB-1…TB-8 register in `04-security-program.md` §4.1 with a new boundary id for the CI/SCM boundary, numbered to follow the existing register.
- **STRIDE enumeration** per boundary, with at minimum these threats explicitly analysed:
  - **S**: impersonating a code-owner approval; forging a QA/security sign-off by typing a marker into an issue body; a spoofed commit author identity (unsigned commits).
  - **T**: modifying `.github/workflows/` to disable a guard; weakening branch protection in the UI; tampering with `CONSTITUTION.md` to retro-justify a bypass; poisoning a third-party Action by floating tag.
  - **R**: an admin disabling and re-enabling protection with no record; a break-glass merge with no audit trail.
  - **I**: a secret leaked into logs by a workflow; a credential pasted into an issue body; repository contents exposed through an over-permissive workflow.
  - **D**: a required check that never reports blocking all merges; a guard credential expiring and failing closed indefinitely; CI exhaustion by a runaway workflow.
  - **E**: `pull_request_target` pwn-request giving a fork PR write access; an over-scoped PAT; a workflow with `permissions: write-all`; a compromised dependency of a checker script.
- **Risk rating** per threat using the same scale as `04-security-program.md` §5.11, with the existing risk-summary table extended.
- **Control mapping**: each threat mapped to a specific control shipped by this epic (E01-T04 ownership totality, E01-T07 fail-closed actor-attributed guards, E01-T08 `enforce_admins` + drift detection, E01-Q02 canary self-tests + weekly drift job, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions) or to an accepted risk with a dated owner sign-off.
- **New security requirements** (`SR-xxx` ids continuing the existing numbering in `04-security-program.md` §6.13/§6.14) for anything the epic's current design does not yet cover — e.g. commit signing, Actions SHA-pinning as a policy, a required-approval environment for admin-credential workflows.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable-style scenarios for QA/security to attempt (feeding E01-X02 and E01-Q01's charter).

## Out of scope

- Product-runtime threat models (keys, OMS, fan-out, RBAC) — already modelled in `04-security-program.md` §5.1–§5.10 and owned by E08/E09/E27/E29/E34.
- Implementing the controls — E01-T04/T07/T08/Q02 and E03.
- Pen-testing — R4 / E43.
- Threat-modelling the Electron shell, network or storage — existing areas, other epics.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is enumerated for the new surface
  Given the development, CI and governance surface
  When the threat model is reviewed
  Then each of Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege has at least one analysed threat
  And each threat has a risk rating on the same scale as the existing section 5.11 summary

Scenario: Every threat maps to a control or an accepted risk
  Given the enumerated threats
  When the control mapping is reviewed
  Then each threat names either a shipped control with its ticket key, or an accepted risk with a dated owner sign-off
  And no threat is left with an empty disposition

Scenario: The privileged automations are modelled before they are built
  Given E01-T07 and E01-T08 both create privileged credentials
  When those tickets enter development
  Then this threat model is already Done
  And its required controls appear in their acceptance criteria

Scenario: An unmitigated critical threat blocks the epic (failure path)
  Given a threat rated critical with no control and no signed acceptance
  When the epic is assessed for Done
  Then the epic cannot reach Done
  And the gap is tracked as a priority/p0-critical security ticket

Scenario: The pwn-request class is explicitly addressed
  Given the workflows shipped by this epic
  When the model reviews fork-triggered execution
  Then it records that pull_request_target with untrusted checkout is prohibited
  And it names the check or review step that enforces the prohibition
```

## Technical notes / design

Method: a 2-hour STRIDE-per-boundary workshop (Security engineer facilitating; Architect, DevSecOps, and the E01-T07/T08 owners attending), following the structure already used in `04-security-program.md` §5 so the new section reads as part of the same document rather than a bolt-on. Reuse its table format exactly: threat id, STRIDE category, description, affected asset, likelihood/impact/rating, control or acceptance.

Explicitly include **AI coding agents** as an actor class. `AGENTS.md` is a 529-line document that autonomous agents read and act upon, making it an instruction surface with real privilege implications: an agent that obeys a tampered `AGENTS.md`, or that is steered by injected content in an issue body it reads, is a genuine tampering/elevation path for this project. This is not a hypothetical for a repository whose planning artefacts are themselves agent-authored, and the model must state the control (CODEOWNERS on `AGENTS.md`, human approval on every PR regardless of author, no agent-triggered privileged workflow).

Commit signing: assess and make a recommendation with a cost/benefit note rather than mandating it reflexively — if adopted, it becomes an `SR-xxx` requirement and a branch-protection setting owned by E01-T08; if declined, that is recorded as an accepted risk with the reason.

## Test plan

- **Review**: the model is walked through at the Security Review ceremony (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3) with the Architect and DevSecOps; sign-off recorded.
- **Abuse-case validation**: each written abuse case is attempted on a scratch repository by E01-X02/E01-Q01 and the observed outcome recorded against the predicted control — a control that does not actually stop its abuse case is a defect in the control, filed as a bug.
- **Traceability check**: every control named in the model resolves to a real ticket key in this epic or to an existing `SR-xxx` requirement.
- No unit tests (analysis artefact). Coverage: N/A.

## Security notes

This ticket *is* the security analysis. Its own risks: (a) a threat model that is written and then never revisited becomes false assurance — mitigated by a stated review trigger (re-review on any change to `.github/workflows/`, branch protection, or the credential set, and at the R4 live-enablement gate); (b) the model itself names attack paths, so it is kept in the private repository and must not include real credential identifiers, account names or token values — only classes and locations. Data classification: **internal-confidential** (attack-path detail), stored in the private repo only. Sign-off: Security engineer (author) + Architect + Owner `@basiltt`, as `04-security-program.md` is co-owned.

## Accessibility notes

N/A for the analysis itself. The document contribution follows the governance markdown conventions (single H1 context, nested headings, header-row tables, prose adjacent to any diagram) verified in E01-D02.

## Performance notes

N/A — no runtime component. One denial-of-service threat carries a performance dimension and must be analysed: a required check that never reports, or a governance job that grows past its 60 s budget, degrades into a delivery-availability problem; the model records that as a D-category threat with E01-Q02's duration budget as its control.

## Observability

The model must specify, per threat, **how we would know it happened** — this is its most operationally useful output: branch-protection drift → weekly drift job (E01-T08/Q02); workflow disabled → drift job's workflow-enabled check; guard credential expiry → fail-closed blocking plus the drift job; secret in logs → `secrets-scan` plus log redaction policy; unreviewed merge → git history audit. Threats with no detection path are called out explicitly as blind spots and either given one or accepted in writing.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] §5.12 (Area 11) added to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; boundary register §4.1 and risk summary §5.11 extended consistently.
- [ ] All STRIDE categories enumerated; every threat rated and dispositioned (control or dated accepted risk).
- [ ] New `SR-xxx` requirements added with ids continuing the existing numbering; no renumbering of existing requirements.
- [ ] Abuse cases written and handed to E01-X02 and E01-Q01.
- [ ] Detection path (or explicit blind-spot acceptance) recorded per threat.
- [ ] AI-agent actor class analysed with its controls.
- [ ] Commit-signing recommendation recorded (adopt with an `SR-xxx`, or decline with a reason).
- [ ] Reviewed at Security Review; **sign-off comments from the Security engineer, Architect and `@basiltt`**.
- [ ] Re-review trigger documented.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated with any new epic-level risk.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner (`/docs/plan/04-security-program.md` → security + architecture).

## Dependencies

No blockers — must run first in Sprint 01, because it **blocks E01-T07 and E01-T08**: neither privileged automation should be designed before its threats are known (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff at epic entry, not at epic close). Feeds E01-X02 (which verifies the controls on the shipped workflows) and E01-Q01's exploratory charter.

title: Security review of governance automation: tokens, pinning, abuse cases
body:
## Context

E01-X01 models the threats; this ticket verifies that the automation E01 actually shipped mitigates them. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2 require a Security-engineer review comment before any `security`-labelled ticket reaches Done, and §8 states that anything touching the fan-out safety invariant, key handling or RBAC is *always* treated as security-labelled whether or not the label was applied.

E01 ships three privileged things: the board-guard credential (E01-T07), the repository-administration credential used to apply branch protection (E01-T08), and a set of workflows that run on every PR (E01-Q02). `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13 (supply chain) and §6.14 (secrets in CI and developer environments) state the requirements; nobody has yet checked the shipped artefacts against them. Getting this wrong is unusually costly here: a workflow token with excess scope in *this* repository is a path to modifying the code that will later place live orders with real exchange API keys.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Token/permission audit** of every workflow shipped by E01 (`board-automation.yml`, `governance.yml`, `governance-drift.yml`): confirm an explicit `permissions:` block at job level (never repository-default, never `write-all`), that each granted scope is actually used, and that the least-privilege principle holds per job. Any unused scope is removed.
- **Credential review**: for the guard credential and the administration credential — type (GitHub App installation token strongly preferred over PAT, per ADR-0016), scope set, storage (Actions secret / protected environment), who can read it, rotation interval and named rotation owner, revocation procedure, and blast radius if leaked. Recorded in a short table appended to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.14's secret inventory (that document owning the content per C-16.5).
- **Fork-safety review**: confirm no workflow uses `pull_request_target` with a checkout of an untrusted ref; confirm no secret is available to a fork-triggered run; confirm no step interpolates issue/PR body content directly into a `run:` shell (the script-injection class) — content must be passed via environment variables or files.
- **Action pinning audit**: every third-party action pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment; no floating tags; a pinned dependency list for the Python setup with hashes.
- **Abuse-case execution** — attempt, on a scratch repository, each abuse case written by E01-X01, at minimum: forge a QA sign-off by typing the marker in the issue body; close a `security` ticket using a comment from a non-security member; supply an `a11y` link pointing at an external site; trigger the guard with the credential revoked (fail-closed); attempt to have a workflow print the token to the log; attempt a script-injection via an issue title/body containing shell metacharacters; disable a workflow and confirm the drift job notices.
- **Findings report** with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, each finding either fixed within this ticket (small) or filed with a `priority/*` and blocking the epic if P0/P1.
- **Security sign-off comments** on E01-T07, E01-T08, E01-Q02 and the epic.

## Out of scope

- Reviewing E03's pipeline workflows — E03's own security review (this ticket covers only workflows E01 ships, and says so explicitly to avoid a coverage gap being assumed away).
- Product security controls (key encryption, RBAC, audit chaining) — E09/E27 and the security epics.
- Pen-testing — R4/E43.
- Authoring the threat model — E01-X01.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every workflow job declares least-privilege permissions
  Given the workflows shipped by E01
  When each job is reviewed
  Then each declares an explicit permissions block
  And every granted scope is demonstrably used by a step in that job
  And no job uses write-all or relies on the repository default

Scenario: No secret is reachable from an untrusted trigger
  Given all E01 workflows
  When their triggers are reviewed
  Then no workflow combines pull_request_target with a checkout of the pull request head
  And no secret is referenced in a job reachable from a fork-originated event

Scenario: Issue content cannot inject shell commands (failure path)
  Given an issue whose title contains shell metacharacters and a command substitution
  When the board automation processes it on the scratch repository
  Then the content is treated as data and no injected command executes
  And the review records which mechanism prevented it

Scenario: A forged sign-off is rejected
  Given a Story whose author typed the QA sign-off marker into the issue body
  When the author closes the issue
  Then the guard rejects the close
  And the abuse case is recorded as passed with evidence

Scenario: The guards fail closed without their credential
  Given the guard credential is revoked on the scratch repository
  When a Story is closed without sign-off
  Then the guard does not allow the close
  And it posts a comment stating the gate could not be verified

Scenario: Every action is pinned to an immutable reference
  Given all E01 workflow files
  When third-party action references are listed
  Then each is a full commit SHA with a version comment
  And no floating tag or branch reference is present
```

## Technical notes / design

Review method: static read of the workflow YAML against a checklist derived from `04-security-program.md` §6.13/§6.14 and the E01-X01 threat list, followed by **dynamic abuse-case execution** on a scratch repository. Static-only review would miss exactly the class of bug that matters most — a guard that looks correct and fails open under a condition nobody tried.

Script-injection check specifically: grep every `run:` block for `${{ github.event.*.body }}`, `${{ github.event.*.title }}` and similar direct interpolation of user-controlled fields; the required pattern is passing via `env:` and referencing the shell variable, quoted. This one grep catches the single most common GitHub Actions vulnerability and belongs in the checklist permanently — propose adding it as a Semgrep rule to E03's `sast` job as a follow-up ticket rather than expanding this one.

Credential preference order to assert: GitHub App installation token (short-lived, repository-scoped, revocable, attributable) > fine-grained PAT (repository-scoped, expiring) > classic PAT (rejected). If a classic PAT is in use, it is a finding at P1.

The administration credential (E01-T08) must be reachable only from a `workflow_dispatch` behind a protected environment with required reviewers, never from an automatic PR trigger — verified explicitly, since that credential can rewrite branch protection itself.

## Test plan

- **Static**: permission-block audit table (job → granted → used → verdict); pinning audit table; injection-pattern grep across all workflows; trigger-vs-secret reachability matrix.
- **Dynamic (scratch repo)**: each abuse case from E01-X01 executed with the observed result recorded against the predicted control.
- **Regression**: every abuse case that can be automated is handed to E01-Q02 to encode (e.g. the injection-pattern grep and the pinning audit become checker steps in the `governance` job) so these properties cannot silently regress.
- **Evidence**: transcripts/screenshots for each executed abuse case attached to the ticket.
- Coverage: N/A (review ticket); any code fixes made here inherit the ≥85% `scripts/` gate.

## Security notes

This ticket *is* the security verification for the epic. Handling rules for its own conduct: abuse cases run on a **scratch repository only** — never attempt to disable protection or revoke credentials on the real repository outside a scheduled, announced window; any credential revoked for testing must be confirmed restored with a recorded post-check, since a half-restored guard credential is a silent governance outage. Findings containing exploitable detail are written in the private repo only and, if a live exposure is found (e.g. a token printed in a public-readable log), the incident path in `SECURITY.md` is followed immediately rather than filing an ordinary ticket. Data classification: internal-confidential. Sign-off: Security engineer, with the Owner informed of any P0/P1.

## Accessibility notes

One adjacent check: security-relevant automation output (a blocked close, a drift alert) must be comprehensible without colour or emoji, since a contributor relying on a screen reader must be able to act on it. Detailed a11y verification of the automation's comments belongs to E01-D02; this ticket only confirms that security-critical messages are not colour-only.

## Performance notes

N/A at runtime. One availability check is in scope: confirm that fail-closed behaviour cannot deadlock delivery indefinitely — there must be a documented, audited manual override (the break-glass runbook from E01-T08), and the review verifies it exists, names who may use it, and that its use is recorded.

## Observability

Verify that each control has the detection path E01-X01 predicted: drift job covers protection and workflow-disabled; `secrets-scan` covers committed secrets; guard audit comments cover gate decisions; log redaction prevents token echo. Any threat whose detection path does not actually work is a finding, not a note — this is the difference between a monitored control and an assumed one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Permission, pinning, trigger/secret-reachability and injection audits complete with tables attached.
- [ ] Credential inventory (type, scope, storage, rotation owner, revocation, blast radius) appended to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.14.
- [ ] All E01-X01 abuse cases executed on a scratch repo with evidence; any control that failed its abuse case has a filed bug.
- [ ] No open P0/P1 security findings against E01 scope.
- [ ] Automatable checks handed to E01-Q02 and encoded; Semgrep-rule follow-up filed for E03.
- [ ] Any test-revoked credential confirmed restored (recorded post-check).
- [ ] Break-glass override verified to exist, be scoped, and be audited.
- [ ] **Security sign-off comments posted on E01-T07, E01-T08, E01-Q02 and the epic** (required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§8 before those can be Done).
- [ ] Findings report committed; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced.
- [ ] PR(s) with any fixes merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T07` (the automation must exist to be reviewed) and `E01-X01` (the threat model supplies the abuse cases and the control expectations — reviewing without it would be an unstructured skim). Blocks the Done status of `E01-T07`, `E01-T08`, `E01-Q02` and the epic itself, since all four require a Security-engineer sign-off comment.

## Branch

`chore/gov-security-review` for the findings report and any workflow fixes. PR size: small.
